f365f1272116e2eb: LIPIS: One person was killed and two others injured when a car skidded and plunged into a ravine along Jalan Utama Kampung Berchang, Kuala Lipis.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department operations and rescue assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call at 9.56pm last night.
A team from the Kuala Lipis Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, about 26km away.
Upon arrival, firefighters found one victim trapped in the car while two others were injured, he said in a statement today.
The trapped victim was pronounced dead at the scene.
The two injured victims were taken to Lipis Hospital.
2020343715e9d803: KUALA LUMPUR: Diver Lee Yiat Qing is keeping her options open for next year's SEA Games as she continues to train in both platform and springboard.
The 18-year-old, who won the 10m platform gold on her SEA Games debut in Phnom Penh in 2023, said her events for next year's edition have yet to be decided.
Yiat Qing did not compete at last year's Games in Thailand, where the individual platform was not contested.
She expects the decision on her events for next year to depend on her performances and believes she could be selected for one or two events.
"For now, I still don't have a clear picture. They haven't discussed what events I'll be taking, so maybe they will decide next year," said Yiat Qing.
Yiat Qing trains with Pandelela Rinong in synchronised platform and Ong Ker Ying in synchronised springboard.

She showed her range at the SEA Age Group Championships, winning the Group A girls' platform event at the National Aquatics Centre in Bukit Jalil on Saturday after taking the 1m springboard gold on Friday.
Yiat Qing scored 358.70 points from eight dives to lead a Malaysian one-two finish ahead of Ng Jia Gee, who collected 345.50.
Indonesia's Nadia Loemongga Sitorus took bronze with 266.95.
Despite the win, Yiat Qing felt she could have done better.
"To be honest, I'm not really satisfied. I was expecting something better," she said.
Yiat Qing, who is competing at her final SEA Age Group Championships, hopes to win gold in all her events before leaving the age-group stage.
She stayed on course when she partnered Teng Hui Xue to win the Group A/B girls' 3m synchronised event in the afternoon.
The pair scored 214.95 points to finish ahead of Singapore's Celeste Liew and Megan Yow (202.65), while Malaysians Ayu Syuhaida Khairul and Mya Yumna Schakeera Suhaili were third with 164.76.
Yiat Qing will conclude her campaign in the individual 3m springboard on Sunday.

Malaysia also took the top two places in the Group A/B boys' 3m synchronised event, with Aeriel Riezqi Abdullah and Lim Zhong Thern scoring 238.32 to finish ahead of Onell Lee and Arif Aisy Rossharisham (236.70).
Vietnam's Phung Chi Kien and Hoang Van Dat were third with 227.31.
Earlier, Arif Aisy led the top three finishers in the Group B boys' 1m springboard with 353.30 points, followed by Afraz Miqael Norazlan (345.75) and Onell (341.55).
Awang Sharzan Zaqwan topped the Group C boys' 3m springboard with 322.30, ahead of fellow Malaysians Cayden Lin (302.80) and Hijri Rayyan (299.15).
Ayu Syuhaida won the Group B girls' 1m springboard with 283.50, just 0.45 points ahead of the Philippines' Adysen Rose Argao, while Mya Yumna was third with 272.15.
In the Group C girls' 3m springboard, Nur Aisy Innara Mohd Amir Hafiz (254.55) and Noor Qaisara Dayana Saiful Nazam (247.20) finished second and third behind Vietnam's Dinh Thi Mai Trang (277.80).

d96db71052d1605c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — The National Early Warning System (MySiren) will undergo a simultaneous nationwide test from 10.10am to 10.30am tomorrow to assess its ability to rapidly deliver emergency notifications to mobile phones.
MySiren is Malaysia’s Early Warning System (EWS), developed to alert the public during emergencies, enabling them to take immediate action to protect lives and property.

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), through the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) section on its official website, said alerts could be issued for serious threats to life, health, safety or property, including severe weather, floods, tsunamis, major fires, hazardous materials incidents and public safety threats.
According to the FAQ, the nationwide public alert test aims to evaluate the system’s performance and identify any technical issues, including how alerts are broadcast and received.
Developed using Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology, MySiren simultaneously delivers alerts to compatible mobile devices in affected areas via 4G and 5G networks without consuming mobile data.

Unlike the Short Message Service (SMS), which sends messages sequentially to specific phone numbers, the technology enables alerts to be received even during network congestion or when users have exhausted their data quota.

MCMC also encourages users to update their mobile phone operating systems, enable their device software features, restart their phones after updating and ensure that emergency alert settings are activated.

“The minimum device requirements to support EWS alerts are iPhone 11 and newer models running iOS 27.2 or later, Android phones running Android 12 or later, and Huawei devices running EMUI 16 or later, subject to final technical verification,” MCMC said.

Authorised disaster management agencies can issue six categories of alerts according to the nature and severity of emergencies, namely National Alert, Extreme Alert, Severe Alert, Missing Person Alert, Test Alert and Exercise Alert.
On November 23, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MySiren only delivers notifications to users without accessing the personal data of device owners.
“MySiren differs from SMS, whereby messages are sent to recipients’ phone numbers, as the system does not retrieve any information or data from users’ devices.
“It also does not involve any cost to recipients,” he said.
Fahmi said the alert test aimed to familiarise the public with MySiren’s distinctive warning sound, thereby enhancing their emergency preparedness.

He said MCMC remained the agency responsible for operating MySiren, while authorities such as the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and local authorities were also granted access to the system.
The development of MySiren began in 2025 at a total cost of RM200 million following an announcement by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2025 in October 2024.

For official information and the latest developments on MySiren, visit www.mcmc.gov.my/mysiren and refer to the official communication channels of MCMC, Nadma and other relevant authorities. — Bernama
c1b9ed2c3213c419: KOTA KINABALU: Three brothers from a farming family in Tenom made their parents proud by earning their Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees together at Universiti Malaysia Sabah's (UMS) 28th Convocation Ceremony today.
The siblings, Wong Vui Keong, 32, and his 30-year-old twin brothers, Vui Ken and Vui Chen, were among 5,081 graduates at the four-day ceremony.
Vui Keong described himself and his twin brothers as their family's "Sentuhan Rezeki", or "lucky charms", a playful nickname given by relatives who believe touching the trio could bring good fortune.
"Our family members say they want to touch us whenever they see us because they can get 'rezeki' or good luck from us," he told reporters after receiving their scrolls.
The eldest of six brothers said their achievement was particularly meaningful given their family's financial struggles.
Coming from a farming family in Kampung Nuluyan, Tenom, the brothers had to largely finance their own studies, which cost tens of thousands of ringgit.
Vui Keong said all three secured part-time tutoring jobs at their faculty to pay their tuition fees.
"We earned our own income and paid our tuition fees. If our parents had extra money, we would ask them for help, but we supported ourselves because we knew it was difficult for our family," he said.
He said he switched to part-time study in his third or fourth year, extending his PhD studies to about seven years.
Vui Keong, who graduated with a PhD in Financial Economics, said the brothers had not planned to complete their studies at the same time.
"We did not plan it, but coincidentally, all three of us graduated together. We are quite excited and happy because we can make our parents proud," he said.
The brothers hope to pursue academic careers and have applied for lecturer positions at UMS and other higher education institutions.
Their father, Wong Yun Loi, 68, said his three youngest sons' achievement was the proudest moment of his life.
73b3e928b97d6de5: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 4,700 creative industry practitioners, including 200 veteran artistes, have benefited from social security coverage under a joint initiative by the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) and the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) between 2024 and 2026.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative reflected the government's commitment to safeguarding the welfare of creative industry practitioners, including those working behind the scenes, through the country's social protection system.
"The welfare of creative industry practitioners working behind the scenes must also be safeguarded," he said in a Facebook post today.

Fahmi said the Finas-Perkeso initiative had helped widen access to social protection for those in the creative industry, noting that in 2022, there was no specific initiative to sponsor Perkeso contributions for the group.

In April 2024, Finas announced RM104,850 in sponsorship for contributions under Perkeso's Self-Employment Social Security Scheme (SKSPS), benefiting 4,500 creative industry practitioners through a collaboration between the Communications Ministry and the Human Resource Ministry.
The scheme provides self-employed individuals with protection against work-related injuries, including accidents and occupational diseases arising from their work activities.
It also offers medical benefits, temporary and permanent disablement benefits, as well as dependants' benefits in the event of death resulting from an employment injury.

1723566ad5b21754: BALING, Nov 28 — Police have identified the mastermind of a drug syndicate involving Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, but he got away just as officers came to arrest him,
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said, the New Straits Times reported today.

“We have identified the mastermind, but when the police went to arrest him, he slipped away. He is on the police radar,” he was quoted as telling reporters after the Immigration Department’s Jelajah Wira Madani programme here.

He added that efforts to track the mastermind are continuing, and that police had mapped out the roles of every suspect in the network, including financiers, transporters, couriers, informants and coordinators.
He said other suspects were also being hunted.

Saifuddin Nasution was also asked if the syndicate was linked to drug networks in the Golden Triangle, a major drug-producing region comprising Myanmar, Laos and Thailand, and replied that the possibility could not be ruled out.

The Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department arrested another RMAF officer and four civilians yesterday, bringing the total number of arrests in the case to 18, including eight RMAF officers and personnel, the newspaper reported.

Three RMAF officers and three civilians were also charged yesterday at the Magistrates’ Court in Shah Alam, Selangor, with trafficking 96.2kg of methamphetamine at the Subang air base at 6.50pm on November 17.

The syndicate was uncovered when 96.64kg of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million, along with 6.98kg of chemical substances, was found during routine screening before the items were loaded onto an RMAF aircraft at the base.
9c7ac9c0864f56dd: KUCHING: After a decade, Sarawak political figures Chong Chieng Jen and Wilfred Yap Yau Sin are set to face off again for the Kota Sentosa seat in the 13th Sarawak state election, in a three-cornered contest that also features a Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) candidate.

Chong, who is also Sarawak DAP chairman, is returning to Kota Sentosa in a bid to reclaim the seat he held for three terms, while Wilfred of Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) faces the challenge of defending the seat he won in 2021.
Joining the contest against the two lawyers is PBK candidate Leu Cheng Hing.
The candidates were announced by Kota Sentosa Returning Officer Mohd Hazwan Othman at the Kota Sentosa Public Library nomination centre.
The rematch between Chong and Wilfred has made Kota Sentosa one of the seats to watch in this election, with both having previously won the constituency.
Chong and Wilfred first faced each other in Kota Sentosa in the 2016 state election, which Chong won with a majority of 2,819 votes.
Wilfred reclaimed the seat in the 2021 election, defeating DAP candidate Michael Kong Feng Nian by a majority of 1,683 votes.
Speaking to reporters after nominations closed, Wilfred stressed his commitment to continuing development in the constituency, citing his five-year track record of service.
"We offer what the people of Kota Sentosa deserve. Over those five years, we have managed to bring in about RM200 million worth of allocations to develop this particular area," he said.
Chong, 55, held the Kota Sentosa seat from 2006 to 2021 before moving to the Padungan seat in the previous state election.
Chong acknowledged the uphill challenge of taking on GPS' dominance but said a stronger opposition presence was crucial to maintaining checks and balances in the Sarawak state legislative assembly.
"I think there's no target, but I hope that we can increase our numbers so that we have a stronger check and balance in the state assembly.

"At the moment, 82 is too lopsided, and it is too easy for them to silence us through suspension, and even the time allocated for debating and raising the issues of the rakyat is too little, because everyone is given only 20 minutes," he said.
Meanwhile, Leu, a former software engineer who contested Kota Sentosa 2021 as well as the Stampin parliamentary seat, is once again offering voters in the constituency an alternative under PBK.
Polling is on Dec 12, with Dec 8 set for early voting.

3489af686c0eeeec: SYDNEY: Australian selectors said they "hope it's not the end" for Nathan Lyon after he was axed Saturday for their four-Test series against New Zealand, leaving the veteran spinner's career in limbo.
Corey Rocchiccioli, who is 10 years younger than the 39-year-old, was preferred instead, one of two debutants in a 13-man squad for the first Test starting at Perth on December 9.
A 14th player will be added following the next round of the domestic Sheffield Shield for a Test that will be the first since the "Sandpapergate" ball-tampering scandal blew up again this month.
With out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne dropped, Queensland batsman Jack Clayton, 27, got the nod to replace him and will likely come in a three, allowing Steve Smith to remain at four.
Clayton has been a form player in the Sheffield Shield and won the race ahead Sam Konstas and Jake Weatherald.
It is the first time Lyon has been left out of an Australian Test squad when fit to play since his debut series in Sri Lanka in 2011.
The sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 from his 145 Tests, Lyon has made no secret of his plans to keep going with tours of India and England in the next nine months.
But he has struggled with form and fitness and chairman of selectors George Bailey said it was difficult phone call telling him was out.
He urged Lyon not to rush any retirement call with a five-Test series in India on spin-friendly tracks in January-February.
"Unfortunately, he just hasn't quite had the impact over the last few games that we would have liked," Bailey told reporters.
"We hope it's not the end for him. We see a path. I think he can have enormous value when you project forward to India on a tour like that with his experience.
"We wanted him to take some time and not rush into any decision off the back of this."
Rocchiccioli, who has played multiple times for Australia A, leapfrogged Todd Murphy, Matt Kuhnemann and Mitchell Swepson in the pecking order as his replacement.
"Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well suited to Australian conditions," added Bailey.

Whether he plays remains to be seen with a chance that Australia could go with four seamers on a traditionally bouncy Perth wicket, with Scott Boland alongside Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.
Clayton's debut is all but locked in after allrounders Cooper Connolly and Beau Webster, who featured in the recent South Africa series, were also left out.
"Jack is a well organised player who has performed consistently for an extended period. His game is well suited to complement the rest of the batting order," said Bailey.
Matt Renshaw and Travis Head look set to remain as openers, with Cameron Green at five, Josh Inglis keeping his place at six and Alex Carey filling out the middle order. - AFP
722459ed8858bb37: KUALA LUMPUR: The government continues to strengthen cooperation with government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to expand the social protection network, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah.
The minister said the effort also seeks to expand economic opportunities and improve the living standards of vulnerable communities, in line with the Madani Economy agenda.

"Community development can only be achieved when various parties join hands with the same goal. This spirit underpins cooperation between GLCs, GLICs and the government through the GLC and GLIC Demi Rakyat dan Negara (GDRN) initiative.

"This initiative started as an effort in the face of disasters, particularly floods, and has now evolved into a more comprehensive platform in supporting the country's social and economic development," he said at CIMB's Social Impact Commitment Announcement 2026 to 2030 event.

Quoting the Yayasan Hasanah 2025 report, he said GDRN members have disbursed RM357.85 million for various disaster relief, community welfare, and education programs that have benefited more than 1.33 million Malaysians across Peninsular Malaysia.

Amir Hamzah said that based on this success, the government has introduced the Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), which emphasises efforts to strengthen the social protection network, expand access to economic opportunities, and improve living standards, especially for vulnerable groups.
He said the government wants to ensure that the benefits of the country's economic growth are enjoyed fairly by all layers of society.
In this regard, the minister said the government is focusing on several priority areas that can provide long-term and sustainable impacts on society.
"First, strengthening the care economy and community welfare through better access to childcare, support for persons with disabilities (PWD), community health, and elderly care.
This effort not only improves the quality of life for the people but also encourages economic participation and workforce productivity.
"Secondly, expanding opportunities to improve living standards through education, TVET, entrepreneurship, and job opportunities to develop skills, build careers, and enhance their economic status.

"Third, strengthening community resilience and environmental sustainability. In the effort to drive economic growth, we need to ensure that communities remain resilient and the natural resources we inherit can be preserved for future generations," he said.

In a separate press release, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd said it had mobilised RM5 million through 17 programmes across its four adopted people's housing programme PPR communities between 2025 and 2026, exceeding its original commitment by 38.6 per cent.

The bank has also announced a RM150 million commitment, which forms part of its broader RM200 million commitment regionally, to create positive social impact for over 150,000 beneficiaries in Malaysia through 2030.
"The commitment encompasses CIMB's full spectrum of community programmes nationwide under its social impact platform, alongside the mobilisation of RM25 million in Zakat Wakalah," it said.
e58a9992644022ef: JOHOR BARU: Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) success in winning 29 seats uncontested in the 13th Sarawak election reflects strong unity and understanding among its component parties, Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the development demonstrated strong ties among the parties, particularly in ensuring political cooperation in Sarawak continues to strengthen.
"It shows there is unity among the GPS component parties.

"It is a good sign, especially as BN made the decision early on not to contest in Sarawak," he said at a press conference after opening the 80th MIC annual general assembly at the Austin International Convention Centre (AICC) in Taman Mount Austin here today.

Also present were MIC president Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran, MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, People's Progressive Party (PPP) president Datuk Dr J. Loga Bala Mohan and Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Earlier, Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun announced that GPS won 29 state seats uncontested after nominations closed today.
This election also set a record for the highest number of uncontested wins, surpassing the 19 seats recorded in the 1996 Sarawak election.
e1d1841791c11757: GEDONG: Sahari Pet said Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurances on development and facilities for residents were the main reason he dropped his challenge for the Gedong state seat.

Sahari, 75, said he sought these assurances from Abang Johari before deciding against contesting the 13th Sarawak state election as an independent candidate, adding that the premier's views also influenced his decision.
"I'm giving way to Datuk Patinggi (Abang Johari). He is the highest-ranking party leader in Sarawak.

“When Datuk Patinggi offers his views, I should step aside. We respect him, so we should not mind. We'll just vote for him," he told reporters after nominations closed at the Gedong Community Hall today.
On his initial intention to contest, Sahari said he wanted to ensure the local community, particularly the Malays, received attention in terms of facilities and development.
"Before we submitted the nomination papers, we asked if he would provide facilities for us and he said okay.
When he gave that explanation and said yes, I decided to step aside. We are satisfied," he said.
Returning officer Jamain Wahab announced Abang Johari's victory at 10.05am after no other nomination papers were received for the seat.
Sahari, who was expected to challenge Abang Johari, had arrived at the nomination centre at about 8.20am, accompanied by proposer Rambli Jamain and supporter Jonnie Sahari.

In Lawas, Mohamad Brahim, who filed his nomination papers as an independent candidate for Bukit Sari in the state election, surprised everyone by withdrawing his candidacy 15 minutes before nominations closed, saying he supported incumbent Awang Tengah Ali Hasan's development agenda.
This unexpected turn of events led to returning officer Ladin Atok announcing at 10.10am that Sarawak deputy pemier Awang Tengah, of Gabungan Parti Sarawak, had won the seat unopposed.
Mohamad, 61, told reporters that although he initially wanted to challenge Awang Tengah, he decided not to after considering the district's progress and its need for further development.
This is the third time Awang Tengah has won unopposed in nearly four decades as an elected representative.
The Election Commission has announced that 29 candidates were elected unopposed in the state election.

29cef0ed3543e342: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — The public is encouraged to harness artificial intelligence (AI) technology to verify the authenticity of information circulating on social media, particularly fake content generated using deepfake technology.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said AI tools such as Meta AI on WhatsApp, Gemini and ChatGPT could help users check the authenticity of videos, graphics and other information before sharing them with others.
“We can now use AI to fight AI. WhatsApp has a Meta AI feature accessible from the bottom right-hand corner of the app.

“We can interact with it, forward messages or share content with Meta AI and ask it to assess the authenticity of the information,” he told reporters after the Koperasi TNB ‘Kasih Rezeki KopTNB’ zakat presentation ceremony at Apartment Zamrud, Jalan Klang Lama, here today.
Fahmi said he had used the tool himself after receiving queries about a viral graphic claiming that Kuala Lumpur was among the world’s 10 most dangerous cities.

“So I forwarded the graphic to Meta AI, which informed me that the statistics were not obtained from official police sources and that their source was unknown. Therefore, we should not believe such content,” he said.

On disaster preparedness, Fahmi advised the public to be prepared and not be alarmed when they hear the test alert for the Early Warning System (EWS) via MySiren, which will be conducted simultaneously nationwide tomorrow (November 29).

He said the test was aimed at familiarising the public with the official alert tone so that they would pay attention and take immediate action to protect themselves and their property in the event of an actual emergency.
“Tomorrow’s test is intended to allow everyone to hear and recognise the MySiren alert tone,” he said.
The nationwide EWS test will be conducted from 10.10am to 10.30am tomorrow to assess the system’s ability to promptly deliver emergency notifications to users’ mobile phones.
Meanwhile, Fahmi reminded parents that the Early Schooling Aid (BAP), which has been increased from RM150 to RM200 per pupil, will be distributed starting January 2027.

He said the distribution of aid in cash at schools, as implemented this year, would continue to foster closer ties between parents and teachers, while facilitating two-way communication on pupils’ development. — Bernama
5c6d0101e2cf0711: KUALA LUMPUR: Wee Yee Hern-Vannee Gobi are just one match away from claiming their second World Tour title after storming into the Syed Modi International mixed doubles final on Saturday.
The world No. 61 defeated India's world No. 185 Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram-Reshika Uthayasooriyan 21-17, 21-18 in the semi-finals at the BBD Uttar Pradesh Badminton Academy in Lucknow.
Yee Hern-Vannee captured their maiden World Tour title last month by winning the Super 100 Kaohsiung Masters in Taiwan.

They have now reached their first Super 300 final, where the Malaysians will face one of two Indonesian pairs — world No. 85 Rehan Naufal Kusharjanto-Melati Daeva Oktavianti or world No. 230 Jafar Hidayatullah-Rinjani Kwinnara Nastine — in Sunday's title showdown.

9d854dfc90f20fcc: LOS ANGELES: The San Antonio Spurs erased a 20-point deficit to beat the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 on Friday and punch their ticket to the NBA Cup quarter-finals on the final night of group play.
Victor Wembanyama scored 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, adding two assists, four steals and a pair of blocked shots to fuel the Spurs in the battle between the Western Conference's top two teams.
Luka Doncic scored 31 points to lead the Lakers, but Los Angeles were eliminated from the in-season tournament.
San Antonio advanced as a wild card with a win that allowed Portland – 116-94 winners over the Golden State Warriors –- to clinch victory in West group C.
Seven of the eight quarter-final Cup berths were still up for grabs going into Friday's games.
The Spurs left it late, but after scoring just 38 points in the first half they out-scored the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter to turn the tide.

Stephon Castle led San Antonio's scoring with 26 points, coming up with a pair of big three-pointers in the fourth quarter. De'Aaron Fox and Wembanyama drained clutch free throws in the waning seconds to seal the win.
"We're battle tested," Castle said. "We win big games and we stick together when it's tough for us."
Doncic was involved in a testy exchange with a fan as he left the court, tossing his wristband toward a woman without looking, backtracking to retrieve it and getting a shove from a man next to her.
"I just threw my wristband, like I do almost every game," Doncic said. "And then I heard she didn't want it so I went back to grab it. And then he pushed me. And then I gave it to somebody else."
In the quarter-finals the Spurs will play the Dallas Mavericks, who beat the Phoenix Suns 113-109 to finish 4-0 in group play.
The Trail Blazers will take on the Memphis Grizzlies, who beat Minnesota 114-109 to eliminate the Timberwolves.
In the East, LeBron James scored 21 points with seven rebounds and six assists as the Philadelphia 76ers cruised to a 111-87 victory over the Indiana Pacers and into the knockout rounds.

Joel Embiid scored 14 points and pulled down 11 rebounds for the Eastern Conference leading 76ers, who finished top of East group B and were joined in the quarter-finals by the Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks and Boston Celtics.
Philadelphia never trailed, leading by as many as 32 to reach the Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

"We're in it," said James, who won the inaugural edition of the tournament with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2023. "Everyone knows about the Cup games, and everyone knows the importance of it and trying to play for something."
- Hawks rally -
In Detroit, Isaiah Joe scored 22 points off the bench to lead seven Pistons players to score in double figures in a 113-98 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks, who led by 16 points early.
Atlanta clinched East group C with an 87-86 victory over the Boston Celtics – who still advanced as a wild card.
Jalen Johnson scored 24 points and Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 20 for the Hawks, who rallied from a 17-point first-half deficit on their way to a fifth straight win.
It was knotted at 83-83 with 1:10 remaining, but Alexander-Walker drove for a go-ahead basket, Jalen Johnson blocked a Jayson Tatum attempt in the lane and the Hawks held on.
Absent from the East's quarter-final lineup are the New York Knicks, who won last year's Cup in what proved a warm-up for their first NBA title in 53 years.
Needing a win and for other results to fall their way, the Knicks erased a 23-point deficit to edge ahead in the fourth quarter before falling 108-105 to the Miami Heat. - AFP

2dd4aaa6b93ec994: JOHOR BAHRU: Angkatan Tentera Malaysia (ATM) akan menilai kelayakan anggota yang terlibat dalam salah laku untuk terus berkhidmat, termasuk mereka yang tidak mempunyai bukti mencukupi untuk dihadapkan ke mahkamah sivil atau jenayah.
Menteri Pertahanan, Khaled Nordin, berkata penilaian itu boleh dilakukan menerusi siasatan dalaman pihak tentera, bagi menentukan sama ada anggota terbabit masih wajar dikekalkan dalam perkhidmatan.

Beliau berkata tindakan itu termasuk kemungkinan terhadap anggota yang ditahan dalam kes penyalahgunaan aset Tentera Udara Diraja Malaysia (TUDM) bagi kegiatan berkaitan dadah, sekiranya mereka tidak lagi direman atau dilepaskan oleh pihak polis.
“Kalau ada yang dilepaskan ataupun tidak direman seperti tiga orang itu, mungkin pihak tentera akan mengadakan siasatan dalaman untuk kita tentukan status.

“Mungkin tak cukup bukti dari sudut nak bawa ke mahkamah sivil atau mahkamah jenayah, pihak tentera akan tengok sama ada wajar ataupun tidak mereka ini patut terus berada dalam perkhidmatan,” katanya.
Beliau berkata demikian kepada pemberita selepas menghadiri Majlis Pelancaran Karnival CIMIC Johor @ Pasir Gudang, di TMIYC Pasir Gudang.

Khaled berkata, kementerian memandang serius sebarang salah laku anggota tentera, kerana perbuatan sedemikian bukan sahaja boleh menjejaskan imej pasukan, malah menggagalkan usaha negara menjaga pertahanan.
Katanya, TUDM telah menubuhkan jawatankuasa siasatan bagi meneliti semua prosedur operasi standard (SOP) sedia ada, susulan kes berkenaan.
Menurutnya, setakat ini lapan anggota tentera, terdiri daripada enam pegawai dan dua anggota lain-lain pangkat telah ditahan, manakala tiga daripada mereka telah didakwa.
Beliau menegaskan kementerian tidak akan berkompromi terhadap mana-mana anggota yang terlibat dalam kegiatan jenayah dan akan menyerahkan mereka kepada pihak polis untuk tindakan undang-undang.
Khaled berkata, pihaknya akan memastikan siasatan kes penyeludupan dadah membabitkan anggota TUDM dilakukan hingga ke akar umbi, termasuk mengesan dalang sebenar sindiket terbabit.
“Kita tidak ada niat untuk mempertahankan sesiapa. Sebab itulah kita tangkap dan serahkan kepada polis untuk disiasat. Kita akan pergi sampai ke lubang cacing.
“Kita berharap pihak polis dapat menangkap dalang sebenar sindiket ini, kerana anggota tentera yang ditahan hanya menjadi alat kepada sindiket berkenaan,” katanya.
Semalam, tiga pegawai TUDM dan tiga orang awam didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret di sini atas pertuduhan mengedar dadah jenis syabu seberat 96.2kg.

Semua tertuduh, terdiri daripada Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, Tan Sui Seng, Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin dan Afifah Amdas, mengaku faham selepas pertuduhan dibacakan di hadapan Majistret Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin.
Mereka didakwa mengikut Seksyen 39B(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952, yang boleh dihukum di bawah Seksyen 39B(2) akta sama, dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 Kanun Keseksaan.
754a1db21dd83c21: PUTRAJAYA: DAP has renewed its call to repeal the Sedition Act, proposing a National Harmony Act to address hate speech and hate crimes.

DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said Malaysia already had laws to address offences involving race, religion and the royal institution (3R), including Sections 298, 298A, 504 and 505 of the Penal Code.
He also cited the amended Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act and the Online Safety Act.

Rather than relying on the Sedition Act, he said the government should introduce a National Harmony Act with specific provisions on racial and religious hate crimes, national harmony and reconciliation.
The proposed law should clearly define hate speech and hate crimes, provide for restorative mediation and protect all communities without criminalising good-faith political debate.
Gobind said protecting racial harmony, religious sensitivities and the royal institution was vital, but retaining a colonial-era law was neither the only nor the best way to achieve this.
He said the Sedition Act, introduced by British colonial administrators in 1948, was open to abuse and could be used to silence dissent.
Its broad definition of sedition had also drawn criticism for restricting political discourse, he added.
"Section 3 defines sedition broadly, criminalising acts deemed to have a seditious 'tendency' even if they are not seditious in themselves. Intent is legally irrelevant.
"Such a catch-all law creates a chilling effect on legitimate political commentary and stifles public accountability," he said in a statement today.

On Tuesday (Nov 24), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat that while he acknowledged concerns surrounding the Act, the government had yet to identify a suitable alternative to preserve racial and religious harmony.
"We must replace colonial-era controls with modern, fair and accountable legislation that safeguards national harmony while upholding the democratic rights of every Malaysian.
"We should therefore repeal the Sedition Act and replace it as soon as possible," the digital minister said.

3e2ad09736bb4b52: KUALA LUMPUR: Scholars, leaders and lifelong learners bear the responsibility of preventing the corruption of knowledge by ensuring intellectual pursuits remains anchored in wisdom and moral judgement, said the Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.

Stressing that the consequences of detaching knowledge from its ethical purpose and moral discipline extend far beyond academia into public institutions and society, His Royal Highness said professional competence and ethical responsibility must go hand in hand.

"The goal of education must be not only to expand knowledge, but also to deepen understanding, promote responsible conduct and foster a commitment to serve others. The values of integrity, justice and compassion must extend beyond the classroom, the lecture hall and the research laboratory.

"Knowledge without integrity may become a tool for self-interest. Expertise without ethics may lose sight of its purpose, while professional success without responsibility leaves little lasting benefit to society," said Sultan Nazrin.
His Royal Highness said this in his remarks at the 42nd Convocation Ceremony of the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM).
Sultan Nazrin said it falls upon scholars, leaders and lifelong learners to preserve the relationship between knowledge and sound judgement.

"The responsibility also belongs to the institutions where your work will be put into practice. May the intellectual discipline you have cultivated at this university guide your decisions, strengthen your character and help you exercise your responsibilities with wisdom and humility," he said.

Citing the warning of the late Tan Sri Prof Syed Naquib al-Attas regarding the "corruption of knowledge" and the loss of moral discipline, His Royal Highness stressed that graduates must act as responsible stewards (Khalifahs) whose decisions are guided by justice, humility and wisdom.
Sultan Nazrin also urged graduates not to become arrogant with their academic titles, invoking the Malay proverb ikutilah resmi padi, semakin berisi, semakin tunduk.

In his speech, Sultan Nazrin also described today's convocation as historic and unique, as he was accorded the honour of conferring the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and master's degrees on the graduands, including IIUM's Constitutional Head, the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.
Congratulating Tunku Azizah on earning her master's degree, Sultan Nazrin commended her humility in attending as a graduating student despite holding the highest office in the university.

"She humbled herself to become a student, demonstrating the discipline of a diligent, committed and earnest scholar," His Royal Highness said, while also welcoming the Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, whom he praised as an exemplary husband supporting his wife's academic journey.
7152aa6993ac05eb: KUALA LUMPUR: Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah
received a Master of Arts in Islamic Thought and Civilisation at the
International Islamic University Malaysia's (IIUM) 42nd convocation today.
Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, who officiated the opening of the convocation, presented the degree to Tunku Azizah.

Her husband, Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, their son, Tengku Mahkota Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah, and other members of the Pahang royal family attended the ceremony.
In his address, Sultan Nazrin congratulated Tunku Azizah for demonstrating that the pursuit of knowledge should not be constrained by position or responsibility.
He said her decision to pursue postgraduate studies while carrying out her royal duties was particularly significant, given that she also held the university's highest constitutional position.
Sultan Nazrin also commended Sultan Abdullah for accompanying his wife and supporting her academic journey.

"Tunku Azizah's determination to pursue advanced study while fulfilling her royal duties is an example of the commitment to learning we celebrate on this occasion, and one deserving of the university's recognition," he said.
Tunku Azizah's research was titled "The Hukum Kanun Pahang: A Study of Sovereign Malay-Islamic Constitution" and examined the historical Malay-Islamic legal code of Pahang.
Her graduation was among the highlights of the opening session of the five-day convocation, which runs from Nov 28 to Dec 2.
A total of 5,489 graduates are being celebrated this year, comprising 920 doctoral and master's degree recipients and 4,569 bachelor's degree graduates.
18505ef5311d440e: MIAMI: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi's Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday.
Rodriguez's goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida.

Defending the MLS Cup was the last chance the ambitious franchise co-owned by David Beckham had to salvage its season after falling in the round of 16 of the CONCACAF Champions Cup and in the group stage of the Leagues Cup.
The only trophy that made it into Miami's cabinet this year was the Campeones Cup, the annual matchup between the champions of MLS and the Mexican league.

For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS's top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested.
In 2024 Miami stumbled against Atlanta United before earning their first MLS Cup crown last year.
The star-studded side featuring Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul as well as Messi, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio.
German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar.

"For me, the defeat is totally unfair because I think the team rose to the occasion, we deserved to win it throughout the whole match," said Miami coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez. "The clearest chances were ours, but that's football.
"The opponents defended well, too. Even though Leo didn't have a shot on target, we created a lot of chances."

The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter's defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.
Miami's early exit extends the champion's curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012.
Gonzalez shook up his starting lineup, leaving Suarez on the bench in favor of young Brazilian Riquelme Fillipi in a change that gave Miami's attack a spark in the first half.
But Messi made an uncharacteristic error in the box after a pinpoint pass from Berterame and Columbus keeper Patrick Schulte came up with a series of saves.
Columbus came close to scoring in the 65th when St. Clair saved a header from Gonzalo Tapia and Miami's Micael blocked the quick follow-up from Brais Mendez.
Gonzalez inserted Suarez with 15 minutes remaining, but Miami still couldn't capitalize on their chances. A Casemiro header was disallowed for offside and Berterame missed a header.
In the day's only other contest, Emmanuel Sabbi's 58th-minute goal lifted the Vancouver Whitecaps to a 1-0 victory over Real Salt Lake for a 2-0 sweep of their first-round series. - AFP

e467c4b7a854e079: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — The government continues to strengthen cooperation with government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to expand the social protection network, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah.
The minister said that the effort also aims to enhance economic opportunities and improve the living standards of vulnerable communities in line with the Madani Economy agenda.

“Community development can only be achieved when various parties join hands with the same goal. This spirit underpins cooperation between GLCs, GLICs and the government through the GLC and GLIC Demi Rakyat dan Negara (GDRN) initiative.

“This initiative started as an effort in the face of disasters, particularly floods, and has now evolved into a more comprehensive platform in supporting the country’s social and economic development,” he said at CIMB’s Social Impact Commitment Announcement 2026 to 2030 event.

Quoting the Yayasan Hasanah 2025 report, he said GDRN members have disbursed RM357.85 million for various disaster relief, community welfare, and education programs that have benefited more than 1.33 million Malaysians across Peninsular Malaysia.

Amir Hamzah said that based on this success, the government has introduced the Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), which emphasises efforts to strengthen the social protection network, expand access to economic opportunities, and improve living standards, especially for vulnerable groups.
He said the government wants to ensure that the benefits of the country’s economic growth are enjoyed fairly by all layers of society.
In this regard, the minister said the government is focusing on several priority areas that can provide long-term and sustainable impacts on society.

“First, strengthening the care economy and community welfare through better access to childcare, support for persons with disabilities (PWD), community health, and elderly care. This effort not only improves the quality of life for the people but also encourages economic participation and workforce productivity.

“Secondly, expanding opportunities to improve living standards through education, TVET, entrepreneurship, and job opportunities to develop skills, build careers, and enhance their economic status,” he said.

“Third, strengthening community resilience and environmental sustainability. In the effort to drive economic growth, we need to ensure that communities remain resilient and the natural resources we inherit can be preserved for future generations,” he said.

In a separate press release, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd said it had mobilised RM5 million through 17 programmes across its four adopted people’s housing programme PPR communities between 2025 and 2026, exceeding its original commitment by 38.6 per cent.

The bank has also announced a RM150 million commitment, which forms part of its broader RM200 million commitment regionally, to create positive social impact for over 150,000 beneficiaries in Malaysia through 2030.
“The commitment encompasses CIMB’s full spectrum of community programmes nationwide under its social impact platform, alongside the mobilisation of RM25 million in Zakat Wakalah,” it said. — Bernama
1bc1aeca4fbc9321: SEREMBAN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a thorough investigation into the alleged use of RMAF aircraft to smuggle drugs.
Anwar said this was not an isolated case and should not be taken lightly, considering that it involved the abuse of national military assets for criminal activities.

"Over the past two or three days, there has been widespread news about RMAF using national military aircraft to smuggle drugs worth millions of ringgit. Not once, but dozens of times, 20 times… to ask us to go easy on the matter or close the case, I'm sorry (but I cannot do that).

"If that's how things are, then find someone else. As long as I'm entrusted with the responsibility, I have said that if you want to betray your country, accept bribery, use RMAF aircraft to smuggle drugs, if u want to get angry, so be it… I don't care; action must be taken. I do not wish to prolong this issue, but everyone needs to know," he said at the opening of the Yakin Madani programme themed 'Memaknai Harapan Rakyat'.

Anwar said he had discussed the matter with Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman and sought their full cooperation in restoring the image of the nation's defence institution.
"Some of those involved with the drug syndicate, including (RMAF's) officers, used aircraft at the air base… we must take action, restore its image," he added.

Yesterday, Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said another RMAF officer and four civilians were arrested to assist in investigations into the cross-border drug smuggling operations of the syndicate that exploited military assets.
The latest arrests brought the total number of suspects detained to 18.

On Nov 17, 11 people, comprising five RMAF personnel and six civilians, were arrested in operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan for suspected involvement in drug smuggling activities using RMAF assets.
Police also seized 96.64kg of drugs believed to be syabu (methamphetamine) worth RM4.83 million, as well as 6.98kg of chemical substances during the operations.
Three RMAF officers and three others were charged at the magistrate's court in Shah Alam, Selangor, yesterday with trafficking more than 90kg of methamphetamine on Nov 17.

Meanwhile, the prime minister said the government's efforts to combat corruption and misappropriation should not be viewed through the lens of political interests; rather, it is a collective responsibility to ensure that the nation's funds and assets are not misused.
He also rejected the notion that corrupt practices are commonplace among leaders or civil servants, while emphasising that such a culture could damage the nation and hinder development efforts.
"This is not a matter of political parties. Some of my own staff have been arrested and charged. Do I like it? I don't, but I abide by the law, and I want this country to be free from such practices.
"I am concerned about this because I see that some people view this matter lightly," he said.

He said the disclosure of the case should also be seen in the context of the government's efforts to combat leakages and irregularities, which are allegedly occurring in other agencies as well, including the Customs Department.
He said weaknesses in enforcement or misuse of monitoring systems should not give certain parties room to evade inspections and smuggle goods.
c7c62a3909a3cb5f: SEREMBAN: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke declined to comment on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for him to end his leave and resume his duties as transport minister.
When approached by reporters, Loke merely shook his head and raised his hand to indicate that he did not wish to comment on his resignation.
Earlier, while officiating at the Negri Sembilan-level Majlis Yakin Madani at the Paroi Youth and Sports Complex, Anwar said he could not accept Loke's decision.
"I find it difficult to accept his proposal to resign, even though he gave his reasons.
"I understand, but I said no reason can outweigh our role in dedicating our duty and responsibility to the people and the nation.
"He is currently on leave, and I want him to resume work as soon as possible," Anwar said.

Loke announced his resignation as transport minister on Nov 10 after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was allowed to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.
The decision was in line with DAP's stance, which had earlier expressed disagreement with the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
Anwar had previously said he had not accepted Loke's resignation and asked him to take leave while the matter was being discussed.
3d5e4480c4e8efe8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Weightlifting Federation (MWF) will rely on coaches Rizal Ruslan and Edmund Yeo to fill the void left after the death of Sakchai Titajaree.
MWF president Datuk Ayub Rahmat said the association would not rush into appointing a replacement, as both coaches were familiar with the national Road to Gold (RTG) athletes.
He said Rizal was currently overseeing the lifters while Edmund was on leave.
"The RTG athletes were previously coached by Edmund and Rizal, so we don't have a problem for now despite Sakchai's passing.
"Either Edmund or Rizal will take over the responsibilities. As Edmund is currently on leave, Rizal is handling the monitoring of the athletes," said Ayub
Both coaches will oversee preparations for the International Weightlifting Federation's (IWF) first qualifying event for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in Doha, Qatar, from Dec 4-11.
Ayub said the national body would assess whether a new coach was needed after the competition.
He added that the immediate priority was to ensure the national lifters' preparations were not disrupted by Sakchai's passing.

Sakchai's death is another setback for Malaysian weightlifting, which is still coming to terms with the career-ending motorcycle accident involving national lifter Hafizuddin Roslin, who lost an arm in the incident last week.
On the cause of Sakchai's death, Ayub said the association had yet to receive a medical report.
"I have not referred to the doctor or received any report on the cause of his death so far," he said.
Sakchai died at a hotel in Thailand while the national contingent were preparing for the Doha competition.
a7c1d32e102e7948: Exclusive: Uploading of intimate psychiatric information to wider medical records prompts some to shun support altogether Some psychiatric patients are refusing treatment over the NHS adding intimate details from therapy sessions to their medical notes, fuelling fears that breaching privacy is posing a risk to health, the Guardian can reveal. One stopped medical care for a heart condition when he discovered that details of intrusive sexual thoughts he’d experienced as result of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) had been shared with a cardiac nurse. Continue reading...
d9694296b174aeab: TUMPAT: A migrant smuggling syndicate used police-style beacon lights and fake registration plates to disguise its vehicles as police cars and evade authorities.
Two Proton Preve cars carrying nine undocumented migrants from Myanmar and India were intercepted in Kampung Kok Serai early today after crossing the Golok River at Pengkalan Kubor.
General Operations Force personnel from the 7th Battalion (PGA7) seized both cars and arrested the drivers during an operation about 6am.
Southeast Brigade General Operations Force commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said syndicates had used similar tactics in previous cases.
"Beacon lights are only permitted for use by the authorities. However, syndicates use them to make it appear as though the cars they are driving belong to the police," he said.
One of the drivers, a 27-year-old Rohingya man believed to be a land-based smuggling agent, narrowly missed enforcement personnel during the operation.
The second car, driven by a Myanmar man, skidded off the road and crashed into a tree.
The nine migrants, including a woman, were aged between 21 and 35 and were to be taken to Kuala Lumpur.
Investigators found that each Myanmar migrant had paid about RM6,000 to enter the country and had been promised jobs in the Klang Valley.
0c14850872c3a4fe: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Malaysia reinforces its standing as a trusted global hub for international dispute resolution following the successful hosting of the third meeting of the Conciliation Commission between Cambodia and Thailand at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) here from November 24 to 27, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

In a statement today, she said the proceedings, held under Annex V of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), culminated in positive technical progress and joint consent for a site visit by the commission.

She said the choice of AIAC as the venue for the inter-state conciliation proceedings demonstrated international confidence in Malaysia as a neutral, secure and conducive environment for constructive engagement.

“The choice of AIAC, being an independent international organisation, as the venue of inter-state conciliation proceedings reflects its capacity to support complex international proceedings and reinforces Malaysia’s standing as a trusted global hub for international dispute resolution,” she said.

According to Azalina, a November 27 press release by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) had announced the conclusion of the third session, which came after earlier meetings held in Singapore from September 14 to 16 and in The Hague, the Netherlands, from October 14 to 18.

She thanked the PCA for its close cooperation with Malaysia in facilitating the hosting at AIAC, adding that Malaysia looks forward to building on the partnership under the Host Country Agreement to advance international dispute resolution.

“Guided by its respect for the rule of law and public international law, Malaysia remains committed to the peaceful settlement of disputes, serving as a neutral seat for international arbitration and a trusted venue for all forms of alternative dispute resolution,” she said.
Azalina also expressed her appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and members of the Cabinet for their unwavering support in facilitating the third meeting in Kuala Lumpur. — Bernama
24c2c8d5b4263e3f: JOHOR BARU: MIC has called for the constitutional powers of the Malay Rulers, which it claims were unconstitutionally curtailed, to be restored.

MIC president Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran said the Federal Constitution was not drafted by a single party or institution, but was born out of negotiations and mutual understanding among the Malay Rulers, community representatives and the British government.

He said Article 38(4) of the Federal Constitution states that no law directly affecting the privileges, position, honours or dignities of the Rulers shall be passed without the consent of the Conference of Rulers.
Article 159(5), meanwhile, stipulates that amendments to certain provisions affecting the position of the Rulers also require such consent, he said.

"However, during the 1993 constitutional amendments, parliamentary Hansard records show that the Dewan Rakyat Speaker informed the House on Jan 18 that he had received a letter from the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal stating that the Conference of Rulers did not agree to the bill.
"On Jan 19, objections were also raised in Parliament over the passing of the amendments without the consent of the Conference of Rulers. Despite this being known, the amendment process proceeded.

"The question is, if the Constitution stipulates that the consent of the Conference of Rulers must be obtained, how could that requirement be set aside?" he said when addressing the 80th MIC General Assembly.
"I believe this matter must be given serious attention. We are not talking about restoring absolute power to the Rulers.
"We are talking about respecting the original agreement enshrined in the Constitution and ensuring that the protections accorded to the royal institution are not sidelined," he said.
Vigneswaran said the country had recently witnessed intense public debate over the pardon and sentence reduction involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
"Some support it. Some oppose it. Some question the process. Others raise questions about the powers and position of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"Differences of opinion are part of democratic life. However, behind the debate over a single person lies a much larger question that we must reflect upon."
c2e33daf9d25e1ce: SERIAN, Nov 28 — Mambong is set for a four-cornered contest in the 13th Sarawak state election, including a family showdown between incumbent Datuk Dr Jerip Susil and his nephew, Rangen Jamang.

At the nomination centre at the Siburan District Office, returning officer Ranum Bari announced at 10.37am that Dr Jerip, contesting under Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) banner, will face Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) candidate Rangen, Parti Bangsa Malaysia candidate Diog Dios and Parti Bangsa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS) candidate Sanjan Daik.
Rangen, is a former Sarawak Administrative Officer (SAO) at Padawan Sub-District Office. — The Borneo Post
170891e45b4262c5: PETALING JAYA: Gobind Singh Deo meminta kerajaan memansuhkan Akta Hasutan 1948 dan menggantikannya dengan Akta Keharmonian Nasional bagi melindungi keharmonian kaum dan agama.
Pengerusi DAP berkata, undang-undang itu terdedah kepada penyalahgunaan dan boleh digunakan untuk menyekat perbezaan pendapat.
Ia menyusul selepas Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim memberitahu Dewan Rakyat tiada alternatif sesuai untuk menggantikan Akta Hasutan.

“Perlindungan keharmonian kaum, sensitiviti agama dan institusi diraja penting, namun mengekalkan undang-undang lapuk era penjajahan bukan satu-satunya atau kaedah terbaik untuk mencapainya,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Beliau yang juga menteri digital berkata, Malaysia sudah ada beberapa peruntukan undang-undang untuk menangani kesalahan berkaitan, termasuk Seksyen 298, 298A, 504 dan 505 Kanun Keseksaan, Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia 1998 serta Akta Keselamatan Dalam Talian 2025.
Justeru, katanya, kerajaan wajar memperkenalkan Akta Keharmonian Nasional yang mengandungi peruntukan khusus berkaitan jenayah kebencian kaum dan agama, keharmonian nasional serta perdamaian.

Akta itu juga perlu mentakrifkan ucapan kebencian dan jenayah kebencian dengan jelas, selain menyediakan ruang mediasi pemulihan serta melindungi semua komuniti tanpa menjadikan perbahasan politik yang dibuat dengan niat baik sebagai kesalahan jenayah.
Cadangan menggantikan Akta Hasutan bukan perkara baru. Pada 2012, bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak mengumumkan akta itu akan dimansuhkan dan digantikan dengan Akta Keharmonian Nasional.

Dua tahun kemudian, Majlis Perundingan Perpaduan Negara mengemukakan tiga draf rang undang-undang berkaitan jenayah kebencian kaum dan agama, keharmonian serta perdamaian nasional, selain penubuhan suruhanjaya bagi menyiasat aduan.
Bagaimanapun, kerajaan ketika itu memutuskan untuk mengekalkan dan memperkukuh Akta Hasutan.

Kerajaan semasa pula memaklumkan akta berkenaan sedang dikaji, dengan Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail berkata pada Januari lalu ia akan digunakan secara minimum selagi masih berkuat kuasa.
Pakatan Harapan sebelum ini berjanji memansuhkan Akta Hasutan menerusi Manifesto PRU 2018, khususnya Janji 27 yang menyasarkan pemansuhan undang-undang bersifat menindas.
April lalu, Gobind menegaskan DAP tidak pernah mengubah pendiriannya untuk memansuhkan akta itu, namun perbezaan pendapat antara parti dalam kerajaan perpaduan menghalang janji berkenaan ditunaikan.
c60d12ec4dd4b9cc: KUALA LUMPUR: National men's doubles coach Herry Iman Pierngadi has defended his decision to withdraw red-hot Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King from this week's Syed Modi International in Lucknow, saying the pair need time to prepare for next season.

Herry said the world No. 34 no longer need to focus on Super 300 tournaments and should instead concentrate on next year's campaign, when the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics qualifying period begins in May.
He said a longer, structured preparation block would serve the pair better after they competed in the Super 500 Arctic Open and Kumamoto Masters.
"Aaron-Roy King do not need to go there. Their performances have improved and they need a longer preparation period ahead of next season." said Herry.
He said skipping Lucknow also gives Aaron-Roy King and the rest of the squad time to adapt to the new 15-point scoring system, which will debut at the Malaysia Open from Jan 21-31.
Herry added that a packed schedule without adequate preparation could affect players' readiness, noting that Aaron-Roy King have already played six tournaments in seven weeks.
In their absence, compatriots Wan Arif Junaidi-Haikal Nazri exited in the last 16 in Lucknow on Thursday after losing to Indonesia's world No. 14 Raymond Indra-Nikolaus Joaquin.
3e5db74170075b97: BALING: The mastermind behind a drug trafficking syndicate involving Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel escaped when police moved in to arrest him.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said efforts to track him down were ongoing.
"We have identified the mastermind, but when the police went to arrest him, he slipped away. He is on the police radar.
"A mousedeer may forget about a snare, but a snare never forgets the mousedeer," he said, citing a Malay proverb.
"That is all I can say," he said on the sidelines of the Immigration Department's Jelajah Wira Madani programme.
An RMAF officer and four civilians were arrested by the Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) yesterday, bringing the total number of arrests in the case to 18.
This includes eight RMAF officers and personnel.
Asked if the syndicate was linked to drug networks in the Golden Triangle — a major drug-producing region in Southeast Asia — Saifuddin said the possibility could not be ruled out.
He said police had identified the role of every suspect in the syndicate's network, including its mastermind, financiers, transporters, couriers, informants and coordinators.
Saifuddin said other suspects were also being tracked down.
Three RMAF officers and three civilians were also charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate's Court yesterday with trafficking 96.2kg of methamphetamine.
The officers were identified as Captain Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, 34, Lieutenant Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, 33, and Lieutenant Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, 27.
They were jointly charged with Tan Sui Seng, 48, Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin, 28, and Afifah Amdas, 34, with committing the offence at the Subang air base at 6.50pm on Nov 17.

The syndicate was uncovered following the discovery of 96.64kg of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million and 6.98kg of chemical substances during routine screening of items before they were loaded onto an RMAF aircraft at the Subang air base.
a0d33bd8053bb8a6: PETALING JAYA: The armed forces will assess whether personnel involved in misconduct should remain in service.
This includes those against whom there is insufficient evidence to be brought before a civil or criminal court, said defence minister Khaled Nordin.
He said such assessments could be conducted through internal military investigations to determine whether the personnel concerned should continue serving, Bernama reported.

He said this could also apply to personnel detained in connection with the misuse of Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft for drug-related activities, should they no longer be remanded or be released by the police.
“If some of them are released or not remanded, like the three, the military may conduct an internal investigation to determine their status.

“Even if there is insufficient evidence to bring them before a civil or criminal court, the military will assess whether it is appropriate for them to remain in service,” he said after attending an event in Johor Bahru today.

Khaled said the ministry viewed any misconduct involving military personnel seriously, as such acts could not only tarnish the image of the armed forces but also undermine the country's defence efforts.
He said the RMAF had set up an investigative committee to review all existing standard operating procedures following the case.
To date, eight military personnel, comprising six officers and two other ranks, have been detained, while three have been charged.
Khalid said the ministry would not compromise with any personnel involved in criminal activities and would hand them over to the police for legal action.
“We have no intention of defending anyone. That is why we arrested them and handed them over to the police for investigation. We will pursue this to the very end.
“We hope the police will arrest the actual mastermind of the syndicate, as the military personnel detained were merely being used by the syndicate.”
Yesterday, three RMAF officers and three civilians were charged at the magistrates’ court with trafficking 96.2kg of methamphetamine.
They were Amirul Faisall Rosdin, Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, Arief Fauzan Ali, Tan Sui Seng, Nur Hanis Syafiqah Amin and Afifah Amdas.
f1214982ba20e6af: SEREMBAN, Nov 28 — The federal government has given an assurance that it will provide sufficient funds to pay the salaries of Negeri Sembilan civil servants next January should disruptions to the functioning of the State Assembly affect the state government’s financial position.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assurance was given to safeguard the welfare of civil servants and ensure that their salary payments would not be affected, particularly next January.
He said Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican had been asked to hold discussions with Negeri Sembilan State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim to coordinate the matter.

“I have asked the Treasury secretary-general to call the State Secretary for discussions. I give my assurance that if there are problems with the functioning of the state assembly, I will ensure that the federal government provides sufficient funds to pay their salaries,” he said when speaking at the Yakin Madani ‘Memaknai Harapan Rakyat’ programme at the Paroi Youth and Sports Complex here today.

Also present were Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Negeri Sembilan State Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Awaludin Said.
Anwar said the commitment was not new, as the federal government had previously provided assistance for the payment of salaries and state government expenditure in Kelantan, Terengganu and Perlis.

“If the (budget) issue is resolved, that is fine. But if it is not, I give my assurance because I do not want civil servants to be left wondering what would happen if there is no guarantee that they will receive their salaries in January,” he said.

He said the federal government would continue implementing programmes that had been agreed upon to ensure that the interests of the people of Negeri Sembilan were not affected by the state’s political developments.
Anwar said all planned development projects and public assistance programmes would continue as long as he is the Prime Minister.
He also urged civil servants to continue performing their duties well and with integrity, while ensuring that the people’s interests remained their top priority.
Meanwhile, Anwar wants the processing of all investment applications in Negeri Sembilan to be expedited, as some investors have complained about delays following the political turmoil in the state.
He said delays in matters involving the state government, including land-related matters, could affect the smooth implementation of investment projects.
According to Anwar, political differences should not hinder cooperation between the federal and state governments, particularly in ensuring that investment processes could proceed and be expedited.
He said efforts to speed up the approval and implementation of projects were important to generate job opportunities and increase the household incomes of the people of Negeri Sembilan.

Yesterday, six state assemblymen were sworn in as State Executive Council members at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah, replacing the 10 members who were removed on September 20, 2026. — Bernama

27ff5d6466d27736: KUCHING, Nov 28 — A political greenhorn from DAP will try to unseat a two-term incumbent in what The Star called the “Battle of the Sims” for Batu Kawah.
DAP is fielding Sim Kiat Leng, a 37-year-old lawyer, against Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) president Prof Datuk Dr Sim Kui Hian, 61, who is deputy premier in the caretaker government.
The two will fight over a suburban seat on the outskirts of Kuching, where 60 per cent of the electorate is Chinese, according to the newspaper.

Dr Sim, a cardiologist and an adjunct professor at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak, arrived at Kota Padawan at about 8.15am to meet and greet Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) supporters before heading to the Padawan Municipal Council building to file his nomination papers.
Kiat Leng followed a minute behind.
Kiat Leng, who has worked with Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen for the past eight years, said his time on the job had prepared him for the contest.
“I’m ready to contest because of the eight years’ experience in solving the people’s issues,” he said.
“I’m facing the leader of SUPP, who is a deputy premier. It’s a tough fight, but I’ll keep going,” he said.
He declined to rate his chances, saying: “I’m a lawyer and we never tell our client that ‘you’ll surely win (the case)’.”
Dr Sim, for his part, urged voters to back GPS to speed up changes in Batu Kawah over the next five years.
SUPP held Batu Kawah from 1970 until DAP took it in 2011.
Dr Sim won it back in 2016 with a 2,085-vote majority over then DAP incumbent Christina Chiew.
In 2021, he held it in a four-cornered contest against DAP’s Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii, Parti Bumi Kenyalang’s Chai Kueh Khun and Aspirasi’s Fong Pau Teck.
Dr Sim polled 7,827 of the 11,150 votes cast, or about 70 per cent, for a majority of 5,393.
b33c1db5247a7171: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Remember the camouflaged BYD Sealion 8 that was spotted testing around Ara Damansara earlier this month? Well, you can now see it up close in person.

BYD Malaysia and Sime Motors have brought out the upcoming three-row flagship SUV for its first official Malaysian public appearance — still wearing its camouflage wrap. The preview is taking place during the BYD Year-End Grand Finale Sale, which runs from November 27 to 29 at the Matrade KL’s Outdoor Exhibition Area.
Sharing the spotlight with BYD’s heavy hitters

The Sealion 8 is not the only headline-grabbing vehicle on display at Matrade KL. The camouflaged SUV shares the exhibition floor with the BYD Shark 6 PHEV pickup truck, the Denza N9 PHEV SUV, as well as the Yangwang U8 electric hypercar and U9 luxury off-roader EREV.

Its public appearance comes hot on the heels of BYD and Sime Motors confirming their local assembly (CKD) plans at the Inokom plant in Kulim, Kedah — which kicks off with the BYD Shark 6 plug-in hybrid pickup. However, neither BYD Malaysia nor Sime Motors has released any official specifications, variant details, or launch timeline for the Sealion 8 so far.
What the camo unit tells us so far

Even under full camouflage, key exterior cues — most notably the dual rear-fender flaps housing a fuel filler door on one side and a charging port on the other — identify the Malaysian preview unit as the plug-in hybrid (PHEV) version of the Sealion 8, rather than a pure battery-electric vehicle (BEV).

Measuring 5,040mm long with a 2,950mm wheelbase, the Sealion 8 is positioned as a full-size, seven-seater flagship family SUV. Based on right-hand-drive (RHD) specifications already launched in markets such as New Zealand, Australia, and Singapore, the Sealion 8 PHEV pairs a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine with either a front-wheel-drive (DM-i) or dual-motor all-wheel-drive (DM-p) setup:

afbe808d6a46e7ca: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 28 — The Sarawak Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will open five operations rooms for the public to provide information and lodge complaints on corruption and abuse of power throughout the Sarawak state election.

8a4bfa3c693dcf62: KUALA LUMPUR: Three-time Olympic diver Nur Dhabitah Sabri and her husband, comedian Aizat Ahmad Nazri, have welcomed their first child, a baby boy.

3674bf6653852fc1: KUALA SELANGOR: The Health Ministry (MOH) is investigating a food poisoning incident involving students at a school in Kuala Langat.
