d13bbfc0ab913da4: PETALING JAYA: DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo has called for the Sedition Act to be repealed and replaced with a National Harmony Act, after Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat there was no suitable alternative.
Gobind said DAP remained firm in its call to abolish the 1948 law, which he said was open to abuse and could be used to silence dissent.
"A catch-all law that polices perceived 'tendency' rather than actual harm creates a chilling effect on legitimate political commentary and stifles public accountability," he said in a statement.
He said protecting racial harmony, religious sensitivities and the royal institution was important, but retaining an outdated colonial law was not the only, or the best way, to do so.

Gobind, who is also digital minister, pointed out that Malaysia already had several laws to address such offences, including Sections 298, 298A, 504 and 505 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and the Online Safety Act 2025.
As such, he said the government should introduce a dedicated National Harmony Act, comprising specific provisions on racial and religious hate crimes, national harmony and reconciliation.

The proposed framework should clearly define hate speech and hate crimes, provide for restorative mediation and protect all communities equally without criminalising good-faith political debate, he said.
The idea of a National Harmony Act is not new. In 2012, then prime minister Najib Razak announced that the Sedition Act would be repealed and replaced with such a law.

Two years later, the National Unity Consultative Council proposed three draft bills covering racial and religious hate crimes, national harmony and reconciliation, and the establishment of a commission to investigate complaints.
However, the government later decided to retain and strengthen the Sedition Act instead.
The current government has said that the Sedition Act is being reviewed, with home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail saying in January that it would be used sparingly while it remained in force.
Pakatan Harapan had pledged to repeal the Sedition Act in its 2018 general election manifesto, under Promise 27, which called for the abolition of oppressive laws.
Gobind said in April that DAP had not changed its position on abolishing the Act, but disagreements among parties in the unity government had prevented the pledge from being fulfilled.
d602b04866c28ece: DHAKA: Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between Nov 1 and 18, brands diverted about US$254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than US$400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.
Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia also benefit
India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all workers would resume work from Saturday.
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.
Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers' representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh.

He said retailers already factor political instability and labour unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves "hard to justify" and raising "serious doubts" whether the unrest was more than an excuse.

Factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.
Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11% and Trident gaining about 5%. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living, KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers "at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying".
More business at risk
Factory owners said the bigger concern was that diversions of business could become permanent.
Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources.
But Chowdhury said that price became secondary when brands were under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines.
India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.
Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments.
Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.

"Since Nov 1, most of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."
Political tensions surrounding former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.

Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.
"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists."
e0b341599f05f860: SEREMBAN: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim hari ini mahu siasatan menyeluruh dilakukan terhadap kes penyeludupan dadah menggunakan pesawat Tentera Udara Diraja Malaysia (TUDM).
Beliau berkata kes berkenaan bukanlah kes terpencil dan tidak boleh dipandang ringan, memandangkan ia melibatkan penyalahgunaan aset pertahanan negara untuk kegiatan jenayah.

“Ini semalam dan dua tiga hari ini, heboh soal TUDM guna pesawat pertahanan negara, seludup dadah (bernilai) ratus juta ringgit. Bukan sekali, berpuluh kali, 20 kali ... nak suruh kita ringankan, tutup kes itu, saya minta maaf.

“Kalau begini, cari orang lain. Saya selagi diberi amanah, saya dah beritahu, kamu melakukan pengkhianatan kepada negara, rasuah, guna pesawat TUDM seludup dadah, nak marah, marahlah ... saya tidak peduli, tindakan wajib diambil. Saya bukan nak panjangkan isu tetapi semua harus tahu,” kata beliau ketika berucap merasmikan program Yakin Madani yang bertemakan 'Memaknai Harapan Rakyat', di sini hari ini.
Yang turut hadir ialah Menteri Pengangkutan Loke Siew Fook, Ketua Setiausaha Negara Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar dan Speaker Dewan Undangan Negeri (DUN) Negeri Sembilan Awaludin Said.

Anwar berkata beliau telah berhubung dengan Menteri Pertahanan Khaled Nordin dan Panglima Angkatan Tentera Malek Razak Sulaiman bagi membincangkan perkara itu, selain meminta kerjasama penuh pihak berkaitan dalam usaha membersihkan imej institusi pertahanan negara.
“Berapa orang yang terlibat, kaptennya, pegawai tentera dengan sindiket dadah, guna pesawat di lapangan terbang … kita terpaksa ambil tindakan, bersihkan,” kata beliau.

Semalam, Pengarah Jabatan Siasatan Jenayah Narkotik (JSJN) Bukit Aman Hussein Omar Khan berkata seorang lagi pegawai TUDM dan empat orang awam ditahan pada Khamis bagi membantu siasatan berhubung kegiatan sindiket penyeludupan dadah rentas sempadan menggunakan aset ketenteraan.
Penahanan terbaharu itu menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan individu yang ditahan setakat ini sebanyak 18 orang.

Pada 17 Nov lepas, sebanyak 11 individu terdiri daripada lima pegawai dan anggota TUDM serta enam orang awam ditahan dalam operasi di Lembah Klang dan Labuan kerana disyaki terbabit aktiviti penyeludupan dadah menggunakan aset TUDM.
Polis turut merampas 96.64 kg dadah disyaki syabu bernilai RM4.83 juta serta 6.98 kg bahan kimia dalam operasi berkenaan.

Selain itu, tiga pegawai TUDM dan tiga individu lain turut dihadapkan ke Mahkamah Majistret Shah Alam, Selangor semalam atas pertuduhan mengedar lebih 90 kg dadah jenis methamphetamine pada 17 Nov lepas.

Dalam pada itu, perdana menteri menegaskan bahawa usaha kerajaan untuk membanteras rasuah dan penyelewengan tidak seharusnya dilihat berdasarkan kepentingan politik, sebaliknya menjadi tanggungjawab bersama untuk memastikan wang dan aset negara tidak disalahgunakan.

Beliau turut menolak tanggapan bahawa amalan rasuah merupakan perkara biasa dalam kalangan pemimpin atau penjawat awam, selain menegaskan budaya sedemikian boleh merosakkan negara dan menjejaskan usaha pembangunan.
“Ini bukan soal parti. Staf saya ada yang ditangkap dan didakwa. Apakah saya suka? Saya tak suka, tapi saya patuh kepada undang-undang dan saya nak negara ini selamat daripada amalan ini.
“Saya bimbang hal ini kerana saya lihat ada sebahagian daripada rakyat kita pandang ringan,” kata beliau.

Anwar berkata pendedahan kes berkenaan juga perlu dilihat dalam konteks usaha kerajaan membanteras kebocoran dan penyelewengan yang didakwa turut berlaku dalam agensi lain, termasuk Jabatan Kastam Diraja Malaysia (JKDM).

Beliau berkata kelemahan penguatkuasaan atau penyalahgunaan sistem pemantauan tidak seharusnya dijadikan ruang oleh pihak tertentu untuk mengambil kesempatan bagi mengelak pemeriksaan dan menyeludup barangan.

Perdana Menteri berkata usaha memelihara integriti dan membanteras amalan yang merosakkan tatakelola negara perlu menjadi tanggungjawab semua pihak dan memastikan dasar kerajaan dilaksanakan dengan berpegang kepada prinsip amanah.
06e842eab2472d1a: GEDONG, Nov 28 — Independent candidates who contest against Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) cannot be considered aligned with the coalition, said Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.

Responding to a question on whether independent candidates who are friendly towards GPS would enjoy any special consideration, including in terms of constituency allocations, the coalition chairman said political discipline remained important within an organisation.
“If they are friendly towards GPS, we appreciate that. However, if they contest outside GPS, it means they are not aligned with GPS,” he told a press conference here after winning the seat unopposed.
Asked whether this meant such candidates should be regarded as opposition, Abang Johari replied: “That is up to you to interpret.”
He said this was in line with the importance of maintaining discipline within a political organisation.

His remarks came amid the emergence of several independent candidates in the 13th state election, including individuals with previous ties to GPS component parties or those who have expressed support for Abang Johari’s leadership.

Among them is former Ngemah assemblyman Anyi Jana, who left Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) after being dropped from the coalition’s candidate line-up and is contesting as an independent against GPS candidate Alexander Donald.
In Simanggang, Wilson Entebang is also contesting as an independent against GPS candidate Leonard Libau Anol after previously seeking to be nominated as the coalition’s candidate for the seat.

The emergence of independent candidates is reportedly largely due to internal party dynamics and dissatisfaction over candidate selection, particularly among individuals who had hoped to secure GPS nominations.
The coalition is fielding candidates in all 82 constituencies in the election, with polling scheduled for December 12. — The Borneo Post
0d7db648eb5ee53b: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 28 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) will assess whether personnel involved in misconduct should remain in service, including those against whom there is insufficient evidence to be brought before a civil or criminal court.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such assessments could be conducted through internal military investigations to determine whether the personnel concerned should continue serving.

He said this could also apply to personnel detained in connection with the misuse of Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) assets for drug-related activities, should they no longer be remanded or be released by the police.
“If some of them are released or not remanded, like the three, the military may conduct an internal investigation to determine their status.
“Even if there is insufficient evidence to bring them before a civil or criminal court, the military will assess whether it is appropriate for them to remain in service,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the launch of the CIMIC Johor @ Pasir Gudang Carnival at TMIYC Pasir Gudang.

Mohamed Khaled said the ministry viewed any misconduct involving military personnel seriously, as such acts could not only tarnish the image of the armed forces but also undermine the country’s defence efforts.
He said the RMAF had set up an investigative committee to review all existing standard operating procedures (SOPs) following the case.
To date, eight military personnel, comprising six officers and two other ranks, have been detained, while three have been charged.
He stressed that the ministry would not compromise with any personnel involved in criminal activities and would hand them over to the police for legal action.
He said the ministry would ensure that the investigation into the drug smuggling case involving RMAF personnel was pursued thoroughly, including identifying the syndicate’s actual mastermind.
“We have no intention of defending anyone. That is why we arrested them and handed them over to the police for investigation. We will pursue this to the very end.
“We hope the police will arrest the actual mastermind of the syndicate, as the military personnel detained were merely being used by the syndicate,” he said.
Yesterday, three RMAF officers and three civilians were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here with trafficking 96.2 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine.
They were Captain Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, Lieutenant Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, Lieutenant Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, Tan Sui Seng, Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin and Afifah Amdas.
They were charged under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

e620fd55452c2c15: PETALING JAYA: CIMB Group Holdings Berhad (CIMB) memperuntukkan RM150 juta dalam tempoh lima tahun bagi menjana impak sosial kepada lebih 150,000 penerima manfaat menjelang 2030.
Komitmen itu sebahagian daripada peruntukan serantau RM200 juta dan merangkumi RM25 juta menerusi Zakat Wakalah.

“Inisiatif ini merangkumi bidang pendidikan, literasi kewangan, biasiswa, pembangunan kemahiran, keusahawanan, pemerkasaan komuniti serta bantuan bencana, selaras agenda Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP) untuk meningkatkan taraf sosioekonomi rakyat.

“Antara langkah utama ialah memperluas program perumahan rakyat (PPR) sedia ada menerusi PPR 2.0 yang dijangka memanfaatkan 45,000 individu dan 5,000 keluarga melalui bantuan pendidikan, keperluan asas serta pemerkasaan ekonomi,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

CIMB turut memperuntukkan RM15 juta bagi program pemerkasaan ekonomi yang dijangka memberi manfaat kepada 5,000 individu, termasuk 4,000 golongan kurang mendapat perkhidmatan seperti ibu tunggal, belia berisiko dan orang kurang upaya.
Inisiatif itu juga menyasarkan latihan kepada 1,000 penjaga baharu bagi menyokong pertumbuhan ekonomi penjagaan serta memenuhi keperluan populasi warga emas negara.

Manakala, RM25 juta Zakat Wakalah akan disalurkan bagi pembangunan komuniti, penjagaan kesihatan dan pendidikan belia, termasuk inisiatif pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET), pembangunan keusahawanan serta program keterangkuman sosial.

Sementara itu, ketika menyempurnakan pelancaran usaha berkenaan di PPR Pinggiran Bukit Jalil, Menteri Kewangan II, Amir Hamzah Azizan, berkata komitmen CIMB membuktikan bagaimana penyertaan sektor korporat dapat melengkapi usaha nasional secara bermakna untuk meningkatkan taraf hidup, memperluas peluang dan membina komuniti lebih kukuh serta berdaya tahan.

“Kerajaan komited untuk memastikan tiada individu yang terpinggir dalam usaha menuju ke arah Malaysia yang lebih inklusif dan mampan. Di bawah rangka kerja GEAR-uP, kami menghimpunkan agensi, GLIC dan GLC untuk menggerakkan sumber dan menangani keperluan sosioekonomi komuniti,” katanya.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan CIMB, Novan Amirudin, pula berkata komitmen itu mencerminkan usaha jangka panjang bank berkenaan memperluas akses pendidikan, memperkukuh penjanaan pendapatan dan meningkatkan daya tahan komuniti.
Antara 2025 dan 2026, CIMB membelanjakan hampir RM5 juta menerusi 17 program di empat komuniti PPR iaitu 38.6% melebihi komitmen asal.
Program itu memanfaatkan lebih 10,000 individu termasuk 5,049 pelajar, 3,200 keluarga, 1,210 warga emas, 485 peserta asnaf dan B40 serta 120 wanita berpendapatan rendah.

0b3bea832c3e5138: PETALING JAYA: Bekas ahli Majlis Kerja Tertinggi (MKT) Umno Nazri Aziz menepis dakwaan pendiriannya mengenai pembahagian kerusi pada PRU16 didorong kepentingan peribadi, sebaliknya menegaskan hasrat menjayakan penyatuan politik Melayu menerusi kerjasama Umno dan PAS.

Wan Saiful turut menasihatkan mereka yang berhasrat bertanding menyerahkan soal pembahagian kerusi kepada pucuk pimpinan parti masing-masing bagi mengelakkan pertikaian terbuka yang boleh menguntungkan Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan DAP.

Nazri turut mempersoalkan kewajaran Wawasan bercakap mengenai penyatuan Melayu sedangkan penubuhan satu lagi parti politik Melayu, menurutnya, hanya menambah perpecahan.
Katanya, bekas ahli Bersatu yang benar-benar mahu menjayakan agenda penyatuan Melayu sepatutnya menyertai Umno menerusi gagasan Rumah Bangsa, bukannya menubuhkan parti baharu.

671514abf87a29d2: PARIS, Nov 28 — French electro stars Justice are among the most-streamed artists in the world thanks to their work on global video game phenomenon GTA VI, with the duo revealing to AFP how and why they landed one of the biggest jobs in the music business.

Xavier de Rosnay and Gaspard Augé are known for their house and rock-inflected dance music, with their tracks D.A.N.C.E and We Are Your Friends among the anthems of the noughties “French Touch” electro scene.

Their work on the score and soundtrack for GTA VI, which has broken sales records for a video game, has propelled the hipsters from Paris to a new level of global fame that has seen them top listening charts on Spotify.

Their GTA song Flower in a Hurricane with Tame Impala and SZA, which opens with a 1980s guitar riff reminiscent of Dire Straits, has been streamed around 90 million times on Spotify since its release eight days ago.

“We were given guidelines that were very broad and at the same time very hard to follow, which were: ‘It has to be fun’,” de Rosnay told AFP in an interview. “But in terms of styles and aesthetic choices, we were completely free.”
“If something wasn’t working, we all felt it. When it was working, we all felt that too,” he said.
Rockstar Games, the New York-based game developer, contacted the duo several years ago to ask them to work on the score — the music players hear as they navigate through the game.
The childhood friends took several weeks discussing ideas to make sure they were the right fit.

What Rockstar wanted “wasn’t at all the ‘French Touch’ stuff, nor our more danceable tracks, but more the rock side, and our ability to play around with those kinds of music and bring them into the contemporary context of Vice City”, de Rosnay added.
Grand Theft Auto VI brought in US$3.79 billion (RM15.6 billion) in retail sales on its first day, according to Rockstar, which called it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
Rockstar has also released a special GTA album, which features two Justice tracks alongside music from a range of A-list artists from rapper Travis Scott to Dua Lipa and Burna Boy.
New challenge
The game follows Jason and Lucia, a modern Bonnie and Clyde, as they embark on a life of crime in and around Vice City, based on Miami, to secure a better future for themselves and their infant son.
But where past instalments revelled in mayhem, violence and crime that saw critics worry about its influence on young people, the latest game is seen as more morally complex.
Matching music to the action was a new challenge for the Justice creators, who will release a 50-track “original score” album on December 11.
“The player’s behaviour isn’t exactly the same with the music as it is without it,” de Rosnay explained.
“The music also had to follow the overall narrative arc, meaning the relationship between the two protagonists, their environment, and the crimes,” he added.
“We had to know every branch of every mission and prepare the music so that all possible scenarios were covered.”
Augé said they were enjoying the exposure and their role in making video game history.
“When you release an album, generally people are interested in it for about a week, then they can choose whether to go back to it or not”, he said.
“Here, it (the interest) is spread out over much more time and it reaches people who have never heard of us.”
“Whatever happens, we can tell ourselves that we took part in this, and that’s an enormous source of pride,” de Rosnay added. — AFP

33b1fab235463466: KUCHING, Nov 28 — The 29 state seats won unopposed in the 13th Sarawak state election today set a new record, surpassing the previous high of 19 seats in the 1996 state election.

Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the development was part of the democratic process, as only one nomination paper was received at each of the 29 nomination centres when nominations closed at 10 am.
“In 1996, the number of seats won unopposed was 19, and this time it is 29, making it the highest to date.
“As for who chooses to contest or not, the EC merely provides the platform,” he told a press conference here today.
Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) won all 29 seats unopposed, including Tanjung Datu, Pantai Damai, Demak Laut, Tupong, Samariang, Satok, Asajaya, Muara Tuang, Sadong Jaya, Simunjan, Gedong and Sebuyau.

The other seats won unopposed by GPS were Lingga, Beting Maro, Engkilili, Saribas, Layar, Bukit Saban, Kuala Rajang, Semop, Daro, Repok, Dalat, Tellian, Katibas, Bukit Goram, Bekenu, Lambir and Bukit Sari.
Meanwhile, Ramlan said the EC had yet to assess the potential cost savings or adjustments arising from the absence of voting in the 29 constituencies, with the necessary arrangements to be made soon.
He said following the development, 632,149 registered voters in the 29 constituencies would not need to cast their ballots on December 12.
“Based on our calculations, the 29 seats account for about 30.71 per cent of Sarawak’s 2.06 million registered voters,” he said.
Ramlan advised voters in the constituencies concerned to check their details and obtain the latest information through the MySPR portal to avoid turning up at polling centres on polling day.

Commenting on the referral to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) regarding the issue of securing a simple majority on nomination day, Ramlan said the AGC’s position was that the electoral process must be completed before a government could be formed. — Bernama
41ce243107b740c3: KUCHING: Seramai 139 calon akan merebut baki 53 kerusi dalam PRN Sarawak ke-13 selepas Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) memenangi 29 kerusi tanpa bertanding.
Pengerusi Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR), Ramlan Harun, berkata seramai 168 calon disahkan bertanding di kesemua 82 kerusi, tanpa sebarang pencalonan ditolak.
GPS bertanding di kesemua 82 kerusi, manakala Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS) meletakkan 29 calon dan Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) sebanyak 17 calon.
DAP bertanding di 14 kerusi, diikuti Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) dengan tiga calon dan Parti Aspirasi Rakyat Sarawak (Aspirasi) dengan seorang calon. Turut bertanding ialah 22 calon bebas.
Baki 53 kerusi menyaksikan 29 pertandingan satu lawan satu, 15 pertandingan tiga penjuru dan sembilan pertandingan empat penjuru.
Calon tertua ialah John Antau Linggang, 78, daripada PBDS yang bertanding di Krian, manakala calon termuda ialah Irene Wong, 24, daripada DAP yang bertanding di Pelawan.
Lebih separuh daripada jumlah calon, iaitu 88 orang, berusia 60 tahun ke atas, manakala hanya tiga calon berusia bawah 30 tahun. Daripada 168 calon, 14 ialah wanita.

Ramlan berkata, rekod sebelum ini bagi kemenangan tanpa bertanding ialah 19 kerusi, yang dicatatkan pada 1996. Beliau berkata, kemenangan tanpa bertanding merupakan sebahagian daripada proses demokrasi.
Dalam perkembangan lain, Ramlan berkata kerajaan Sarawak seterusnya hanya boleh dibentuk selepas keseluruhan proses pilihan raya selesai.

Beliau berkata, ia adalah nasihat diberikan Jabatan Peguam Negara selepas SPR mendapatkan pandangannya semalam berhubung sama ada parti yang memperoleh majoriti mudah pada hari penamaan calon boleh membentuk kerajaan.
“Keseluruhan proses pilihan raya mesti selesai sebelum kerajaan boleh dibentuk,” katanya.
Pengundian awal akan diadakan pada 8 Dis, manakala hari mengundi ditetapkan pada 12 Dis.
2cce1e50fca06ce4: PETALING JAYA: MIC has called for a review of the 1993 constitutional amendments concerning the Malay rulers' legal immunity, arguing that the Conference of Rulers's consent was not obtained for the changes.

MIC president S Vigneswaran, who made the same call in 2020, said Articles 38(4) and 159(5) of the Federal Constitution require the conference’s consent for laws affecting the rulers’ privileges and amendments to certain constitutional provisions.

However, he said Hansard records showed that the then Dewan Rakyat Speaker informed the House on Jan 18, 1993, that he had received a letter from the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal stating that the Conference of Rulers had rejected the bill.
Objections to passing it without the Conference of Rulers's consent were raised again the next day, he said, but he said the amendment process went ahead.
“I believe this matter deserves serious attention. We are not talking about returning absolute power to the rulers.
"We are talking about respecting the original consent enshrined in the Federal Constitution," he said when opening the party's 80th general assembly in Johor.
Vigneswaran stressed that MIC was not seeking to restore absolute power to the rulers but to uphold the original constitutional agreement.
"The Federal Constitution must remain greater than the government of the day. No majority is above the constitution, and no constitutional safeguard should be treated as optional," he said.
The 1993 amendment removed the rulers’ personal immunity from civil and criminal proceedings and established a special court to hear cases involving them.

The first bill was passed by the Dewan Rakyat in January 1993, but the Conference of Rulers withheld its consent. A revised bill was tabled on March 8 and passed the following day. The amendments took effect on March 30, 1993.

Constitutional law scholar Shad Saleem Faruqi previously questioned whether the Conference of Ruler’s consent was obtained for the final version of the amendments, saying the issue raises serious constitutional questions.
d5ac26faeec362cf: SELAYANG: Pemimpin perlu melaksanakan kuasa dengan penuh tanggungjawab demi kepentingan orang lain dan bukannya menganggapnya sebagai satu keistimewaan, titah Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.

Mengambil iktibar daripada kajiannya mengenai Hukum Kanun Pahang, baginda bertitah mereka yang diberi amanah untuk memerintah perlu mempunyai akhlak yang baik, bijaksana dan berkeupayaan untuk berkhidmat.
“Kuasa bukanlah semata-mata satu keistimewaan. Ia adalah amanah,” titah baginda, merujuk kepada tanggungjawab yang datang bersama kepimpinan.
Tunku Azizah bertitah dalam ucapan wakil graduan pada Istiadat Konvokesyen Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) ketika menerima ijazah sarjana daripada Sultan Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah.
Baginda merujuk perumpamaan dalam Hukum Kanun Pahang yang menyamakan pemerintah dengan tukang kebun, kerajaan dengan taman, manakala menteri dan pegawai dengan pepohon di dalamnya

“Hukum Kanun Pahang mengajar kita bahawa pemerintah ibarat tukang kebun yang mengusahakan sebuah taman. Mereka menanam setiap pohon di tempat yang paling sesuai. Setiap pohon seharusnya mengeluarkan buah dan memberikan teduhan. Jika sesebuah pohon tidak lagi membawa manfaat itu, sebaliknya merosakkan taman, ia perlu ditebang dan digantikan.
“Ini bukan sekadar nasihat mengenai pepohon. Ia adalah falsafah pemerintahan.”

Menurut baginda, berdasarkan prinsip itu, pemerintah perlu melantik individu yang mempunyai reputasi dan peribadi yang baik, manakala mereka yang diberi jawatan diharapkan bersikap adil, berwaspada, sabar, berani serta mampu memberikan nasihat yang bijaksana.

Tunku Azizah, yang kembali menyambung pengajian secara formal pada usia 64 tahun selepas berehat selama 45 tahun, menamatkan pengajian dengan cemerlang pada usia 66 tahun, menerima Anugerah Pelajar Terbaik dan dicalonkan bagi Anugerah Tesis Terbaik.
Tesis baginda bertajuk ‘Hukum Kanun Pahang: Satu Kajian tentang Perlembagaan Melayu-Islam yang Berdaulat’ disiapkan di Institut Antarabangsa Pemikiran dan Tamadun Islam, UIAM.

Tunku Azizah turut menjelaskan pengalaman sebagai pelajar turut memperlihatkan perbezaan antara memegang sesuatu jawatan dengan memperoleh pencapaian, sambil menegaskan kedudukannya sebagai ketua perlembagaan UIAM tidak memberikannya sebarang layanan istimewa.

“Saya memasuki dewan ini sebagai Tengku Ampuan Pahang. Saya duduk bersama anda semua sebagai seorang pelajar. Saya melangkah ke pentas ini bersama rakan-rakan graduan dan menerima skrol daripada Sultan Perak, sama seperti graduan lain. Selepas itu, saya kembali ke tempat duduk di atas untuk menjalankan peranan sebagai ketua perlembagaan.

“Saya bertukar tempat duduk beberapa kali hari ini, tetapi masih memakai jubah sarjana yang sama. Tempat duduk itu melambangkan jawatan yang diamanahkan kepada saya, tetapi jubah ini melambangkan sesuatu yang perlu saya usahakan untuk memperolehnya.”
Baginda turut menceritakan penyelia pengajiannya memberikan teguran dan membetulkan hasil kerjanya tanpa mengurangkan standard akademik.

“Walaupun selepas senat mengesahkan pengijazahan saya, saya masih tidak dapat memperoleh transkrip akademik sehingga menjelaskan yuran tertunggak. Saya bertanya, ‘Yuran? Bukankah saya sudah membayar semuanya?’

“Sudah tentu saya membayarnya. Jadi, saya boleh memberi jaminan kepada rakan-rakan graduan bahawa saya memperoleh ijazah ini melalui usaha sendiri dan UIAM juga memastikan saya menjelaskan yuran pengajian!” titah baginda sambil menambah perancangan untuk melanjutkan pengajian ke peringkat doktor falsafah (PhD).

Ditujukan kepada rakan-rakan graduan, baginda bertitah ilmu juga merupakan satu amanah yang perlu dimanfaatkan demi kesejahteraan manusia, sambil mengingatkan bahawa ilmu tanpa nilai murni boleh disalahgunakan untuk mengeksploitasi, memecahbelahkan dan memusnahkan.

Baginda menitahkan mereka membawa tanggungjawab itu ke dalam bidang pentadbiran, pendidikan, perniagaan, perubatan, undang-undang, komuniti dan keluarga, serta memastikan ilmu yang dimiliki dimanfaatkan untuk orang lain dan bukannya sekadar memajukan kepentingan diri sendiri.
“Sebelum kita memerintah orang lain, kita perlu belajar mengawal diri sendiri. Sebelum kita menuntut pemimpin berintegriti, kita perlu mengamalkannya dalam kehidupan sendiri.”

dcdd5314fe13858e: LONDON, Nov 28 — Britain’s Princess Catherine is seen brushing away tears in a new documentary about her cancer journey as she listens to messages of support from her three children.

Catherine, 44, who is married to heir to the throne Prince William, was filmed for the highly personal documentary taking part in one of the UK’s best-known endurance events, the Three Peaks Challenge.
Participants in the challenge, which the princess completed in June, climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.
Messages from her and William’s three children — George, Charlotte and Louis — are played to Catherine by her brother in an emotional scene on England’s Scafell Pike peak.
“They (my children) gave me the reason to get out of hospital. They’re going to give me the reason to finish this challenge,” she is heard saying.
“Hello, Mummy. I really love you and I hope you do well going up the mountain,” her youngest child, eight-year-old Prince Louis tells her.
“Remember, I’m always in your heart with you... And remember, I love you really lots and lots, and I give you lots and lots of love. Bye,” he says.
Catherine, also known as Kate, announced in March 2024 she had been diagnosed with an unspecified cancer and was undergoing chemotherapy.
Her diagnosis coincided with her father-in-law, King Charles III, 78, also being diagnosed with cancer.
“Navigating cancer or any long-term illness is a lonely road. But it’s clear we’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone,” she says in the documentary.
A message from Prince George, 13, who calls Catherine “mumma”, is also played to Catherine by her brother James who accompanied her on the Scafell Pike leg of the challenge.
‘Heal’
“We all love you so much and you’re going to do a great job,” George says, adding he has been keeping tabs on her progress through a flight tracking website.
“You look really, really strong. Keep going and we’re right behind you,” he added.
In the documentary, Heal, the Princess of Wales reflects on her cancer experience alongside others going through their own battles with the disease.
A message from Princess Charlotte, 11, is the last to be played to Catherine, who announced she was in remission in January 2025.
“Hello, Mummy. I love you so much. We are so proud of you doing your walk and your challenges. We really wish you good luck and I’ll be cheering you on. See you soon,” Charlotte is heard saying.
“So sweet,” says Catherine, by now in tears, as her brother tells her: “Sorry, William sent them to me and I said I’d play them when we got to the top.”
Cancer support meeting
In other parts of the documentary — which will be broadcast by the BBC tomorrow — Catherine describes her time in hospital as “really tough”.
“It was a really challenging time, but I feel so grateful because it’s really made me appreciate life so much,” she said.

The programme also shows her joining patients and survivors at a London pub for a cancer support group meeting, saying it was “lovely to be able to share my personal experience, but also hear your stories”.
“I haven’t really explored this outside my family walls, really. So thank you for allowing me the time to do that and the open space to explore that.”
Heal will air internationally via NBCUniversal in the United States on November 30, Channel 9 in Australia on December 1 and CTV and Noovo in Canada on December 7.
All funds generated by its distribution will go to Britain’s Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. — AFP

00d5b5ade08ff2d2: NEW DELHI: Indian authorities have found a sample of Bisleri-branded water to be unsafe due to coliform bacteria, a regulatory document shows, the second such finding in recent days on the nation's biggest and most popular packaged-water brand.

In an Aug 12 notice to Bisleri, the document shows, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India relayed its findings to the company and asked it to prohibit the sale of the affected batch, which was manufactured in July.
The sample was tested again for confirmation and was still found unsafe, said a government official, who declined to be named as the results are not public.

Bisleri told Reuters in a statement on Saturday that it had recalled the batch in August on the government's instructions and that "the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample".

But the company said it commissioned independent testing of samples from the same batch, which found they met "the applicable standard for coliform bacteria and all other applicable food safety standards".
"The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review," the company said. "Bisleri will continue to cooperate fully with FSSAI to establish the facts."
The regulator did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Reuters reported on Monday that the agency had found a sample of Bisleri water unsafe and that it would test samples from all bottled-water companies in India.

Bisleri's 20-cent bottles have made the company a household name in India, where poor water quality has turned bottled water into a necessity for homes and restaurants. It has maintained its market-leader position while competing with PepsiCo and Coca-Cola in India's packaged drinking water market, with estimates showing its valuation at more than US$3.5 billion.

5c19df74188a0a88: SEREMBAN, Nov 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today that he wants a thorough investigation into the drug smuggling case involving the use of Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft.
He said this was not an isolated case and should not be taken lightly, considering that it involved the abuse of national military assets for criminal activities.

“Over the past two or three days, there has been widespread news about RMAF using national military aircraft to smuggle drugs worth millions of ringgit. Not once, but dozens of times, 20 times… to ask us to go easy on the matter or close the case, I’m sorry (but I cannot do that).

“If that’s how things are, then find someone else. As long as I’m entrusted with the responsibility, I have said that if you want to betray your country, accept bribery, use RMAF aircraft to smuggle drugs, if you want to get angry, so be it… I don’t care; action must be taken. I do not wish to prolong this issue, but everyone needs to know,” he said at the opening of the Yakin Madani programme themed ‘Memaknai Harapan Rakyat’, here today.
Also present were Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Awaludin Said.

Anwar said he had discussed the matter with Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman and sought their full cooperation in restoring the image of the nation’s defence institution.
“Some of those involved with the drug syndicate, including (RMAF’s) officers, used aircraft at the air base… we must take action, restore its image,” he added.

Yesterday, Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said another RMAF officer and four civilians were arrested to assist in investigations into the cross-border drug smuggling operations of the syndicate that exploited military assets.
The latest arrests brought the total number of suspects detained to 18.

On November 17, 11 people, comprising five RMAF personnel and six civilians, were arrested in operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan for suspected involvement in drug smuggling activities using RMAF assets.
Police also seized 96.64 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs believed to be syabu (methamphetamine) worth RM4.83 million, as well as 6.98kg of chemical substances during the operations.
In addition, three RMAF officers and three others were charged at the Magistrate’s Court in Shah Alam, Selangor, yesterday with trafficking more than 90kg of methamphetamine on November 17.

Meanwhile, the prime minister stressed that the government’s efforts to combat corruption and misappropriation should not be viewed through the lens of political interests; rather, it is a collective responsibility to ensure that the nation’s funds and assets are not misused.
He also rejected the notion that corrupt practices are commonplace among leaders or civil servants, while emphasising that such a culture could damage the nation and hinder development efforts.
“This is not a matter of political parties. Some of my own staff have been arrested and charged. Do I like it? I don’t, but I abide by the law, and I want this country to be free from such practices.
“I am concerned about this because I see that some people view this matter lightly,” he said.

Anwar said the disclosure of the case should also be seen in the context of the government’s efforts to combat leakages and irregularities, which are allegedly occurring in other agencies as well, including the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM).
He said weaknesses in enforcement or misuse of monitoring systems should not give certain parties room to evade inspections and smuggle goods.

He emphasised that upholding integrity and combating practices that undermine national governance is a collective responsibility, ensuring government policies are implemented in line with the principle of trustworthiness. — Bernama

40ffa9f29696dc9a: SELAYANG: Leaders must exercise authority responsibly and for the benefit of others instead of regarding it as a privilege, says Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.
Drawing on lessons from her research into the Hukum Kanun Pahang, she said those entrusted with governing must be of good character, wise and able to serve.
"Authority is never simply a privilege. It is an amanah," she said, referring to the responsibility that comes with leadership.
Tunku Azizah said this in her valedictory speech at the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) convocation where she received her master’s degree from Perak’s Sultan Nazrin Shah.
She drew on the Hukum Kanun Pahang’s comparison of a ruler to a gardener, the kingdom to a garden, and ministers and officials to its trees.

"The Hukum Kanun Pahang tells us: rulers are like gardeners cultivating a garden. They plant each tree where it is most fitting. Each tree should bear fruit and provide shade. If a tree no longer brings these benefits and instead damages the garden, it must be removed and replaced.
"This is not merely advice about trees. It is a philosophy of government," she said.

Under these principles, she said, rulers are required to appoint people of good reputation and sound character, while those entrusted with office are expected to be just, vigilant, patient, courageous and capable of offering wise counsel.
Tunku Azizah, who returned to formal education at 64 after a 45-year break, graduated with distinction at 66, received the Best Student Award and was nominated for the Best Thesis Award.
Her thesis, titled "The Hukum Kanun Pahang: A Study of a Sovereign Malay-Islamic Constitution", was undertaken at IIUM’s International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation.

In her speech, Tunku Azizah said her experience as a student also underlined the distinction between holding an office and earning an achievement, stressing that her position as IIUM’s constitutional head had brought her no special treatment.

"I entered this hall as Tengku Ampuan of Pahang. I sat among you as a student. I walked across this stage with my fellow graduates and received my scroll from the Sultan of Perak, just as every other graduate did. Then, I quietly found my way back up here to take my seat as constitutional head.
"I have changed seats several times today, but I am still wearing the same master’s robe. The seat represents the office entrusted to me, but this robe represents something I had to earn."
She said her supervisors had also challenged and corrected her work without lowering academic standards.
"Even after the senate endorsed my graduation, I could not get my academic transcript until I settled my outstanding fees. I asked, ‘Fees? Haven’t I paid everything?’
"I paid, of course. So I can assure my fellow graduates: I earned this degree, and IIUM made sure I paid my fees, too!" she said, adding that she would pursue a doctorate next.
Turning to her fellow graduates, she said knowledge was also a trust that must benefit humanity, warning that learning without virtue could be used to exploit, divide and destroy.

She urged them to carry that responsibility into government, education, business, medicine, law, their communities and their homes, ensuring that their knowledge served others rather than merely advancing their own interests.
"Before we govern others, we must learn to govern ourselves. Before we demand integrity from our leaders, we must practise it in our own lives."
5485b0332d3129f4: KUCHING, Nov 28 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is increasing water storage at the Pedu Dam in Kedah to ensure sufficient supply for paddy field irrigation in the event of an El Nino phenomenon from late December this year until April next year.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the measure was important to ensure paddy cultivation, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia, was not affected by water shortages.
He said based on forecasts by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), hot weather was expected to affect several states, including Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.
“Currently, the water level at Pedu Dam is good, but we want to increase the storage further to ensure sufficient water for paddy field irrigation if there is no rain from December to April.

“That is why I was at Pedu Dam two days ago to ensure efforts to increase water storage could be carried out,” he told Bernama after attending the Agro Madani Mega Sales @ Medan Niaga Satok 2026 programme here today.
Mohamad also said adherence to the paddy planting schedule was important to avoid water shortages while crops were growing, particularly during a prolonged dry spell.

“We also hope all parties, including the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada), ensure that the paddy planting schedule is adhered to. If planting is not carried out according to schedule, we are concerned that water shortages may occur while the paddy is growing,” he said.

On preparations for the monsoon season, Mohamad said relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Social Welfare Department and the Education Ministry, were always prepared to deal with possible floods.
However, he said El Nino required a different approach as its effects remained difficult to predict, while flash floods had also become increasingly serious in recent times.

“Rain in Malaysia is nothing unusual... the monsoon season is something we face every year, but El Nino is a relatively new phenomenon that requires different preparations because its effects are still difficult to predict.
“Insya-Allah, the government is always prepared for the monsoon season based on past experience. However, El Nino requires a slightly different approach and preparedness measures,” he said. — Bernama
09eccaa2760255b7: SELAYANG: Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah is set to pursue a doctorate at the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) after graduating with a master's degree today.

0d90d60f43efdc36: WASHINGTON: The US military denied Friday any issues with its computer security following media reports that the Air Force's cloud based system was hacked, in what would be the latest high profile breach of US digital infrastructure in recent weeks.

Instead, a Defense Department official told AFP late Friday that "The Department of War's systems are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world. We will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications."
"As a matter of policy and operations security, the Department of War does not comment on the status of our networks," a Defense Department official said earlier on Friday.
NBC News, a major US broadcaster, reported Friday citing an unnamed US official, that the cloud platform had been breached and that an attack "could have exposed sensitive military information."
The breach was first reported by Reuters earlier Friday.
Federal News Network, which specializes in covering US federal agencies, also confirmed the breach, citing a "person familiar with the incident."
The contractors discovered the hack earlier in the year while doing maintenance on the system, Federal News said.
The reported attack is the latest in a string of major outages in US government and private-sector digital infrastructure.
In recent weeks the CIA and FBI were also reportedly subject to hacks.
Suppliers for major American financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard were also hit.

In other instances, such as a major Microsoft Outlook outage, a separate US air traffic control issue and a reported issue with a top-secret National Security Agency (NSA) network earlier this month, officials were at pains to blame the outages on maintenance or defects -- not intrusions.
The attacks and outages are not limited to the US.

bc8b465443e11eae: Imbau kembali. Khamis lalu pemimpin BN diketuai Pengerusinya Zahid Hamidi diterima menghadap Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan dan selesai sesi menghadap, beliau beritahu media yang BN menyerahkan kepada Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir untuk mengumumkan hasil pertemuan.

“Kami telah menghadap Tuanku dalam suasana tenang dan Tuanku akan membuat keputusan dan kita akan serahkan kepada pihak istana yang mengeluarkan kenyataan keputusan yang telah kami capai. Biarlah kenyataan daripada istana itu sebagai memuktamadkan keputusan yang telah kami sama-sama setuju,” kata Zahid.
Bagi saya kata kuncinya 'keputusan yang telah kami sama-sama setuju'.

Tidak ada kenyataan dikeluarkan istana secara khusus tetapi keesokan hari yakni semalam Yang Dipertuan Besar perkenan berangkat ke istiadat pelantikan dan angkat sumpah exco di Istana Besar Seri Menanti, dan Ismail Lasim hadir sebagai atau selaku menteri besar.

This speaks louder than any worded statement. It is telling. Oleh kerana Zahid sebelum ini (seperti disebut tadi) berkata 'keputusan yang telah kami sama-sama setuju'. BN khususnya Umno boleh dianggap akhirnya ‘merestui’ Ismail kekal sebagai menteri besar.

Bukanlah rahsia besar Umno mahu ketuanya di Negeri Sembilan Jalaluddin Alias jadi menteri besar. Maklumlah Jalaluddin watak utama yang berjaya ‘memaksa’ PRN diadakan Ogos lalu. Apa yang beliau (dan Umno) lakukan tidak perlu diulangi kerana ramai sudah maklum.

Namun, hasrat Umno mahu Jalaluddin jadi menteri besar tidak kesampaian dan muncullah the little known 67-year-old Ismail sebagai menteri besar. Ketika namanya diumumkan ramai yang bertanya ‘Ismail who?’.
Ismail kemudian kita tahu bergelumang dalam krisis Negeri Sembilan siap dengan langkah U-turn, penafian dan pengakuan.

Pada 16 Nov lalu, Setiausaha Agung BN, Zambry Abdul Kadir (bukan Ismail ye) mengumumkan Ismail letak jawatan menteri besar berkuat kuasa serta-merta. Banyak spekulasi timbul yang tidak perlu saya ulangi.
Pendekkan cerita yang panjang eventually BN menghadap Tuanku Muhriz yang disebut pada permulaan penulisan ini.
Oleh kerana yang dilantik dan angkat sumpah semalam ialah enam orang, Ismail akan menentukan portfolio mereka dalam sehari dua lagi.
Kata beliau, setiap seorang exco yang baru dilantik dijangka pegang sekurang-kurangnya dua portfolio bagi memastikan kelancaran pentadbiran negeri.
Sebelum ini, umum tahu Negeri Sembilan ada 10 orang exco. September lalu Tuanku Muhriz melucutkan pelantikan mereka kerana ‘melanggar sumpah jawatan’.

Dengan pelantikan enam exco baru Ismail berkata “seawal minggu depan saya telah tetapkan mesyuarat exco diadakan pada Selasa dan Khamis dan mungkin lebih kerap lagi supaya dapat menyelesaikan tunggakan yang berlaku."

Menurutnya, mesyuarat exco akan datang akan mengesahkan belanjawan negeri sebelum dipersembahkan kepada Tuanku Muhriz selain mendapatkan perkenan tarikh persidangan DUN yang dijangka berlangsung Disember ini. Sememangnya Ismail has got a lot of lost ground to cover.

Sengaja saya huraikan itu semua untuk menunjukkan Ismail is the menteri besar and apparently, he is in charge. Saya tidak dapat elak menyatakan apa yang dilakukan Zambry tempoh hari adalah tindakan sia-sia. Apatah lagi mengambil kira apa yang dikata Zahid setelah menghadap Tuanku Muhriz yang disebut tadi.

Pun begitu, jika masih ada rasa tidak puas hati dalam kalangan Umno terhadap Ismail eloklah teliti titah Yang Dipertuan Besar. Saya kira titah Tuanku Muhriz pada istiadat pelantikan dan angkat sumpah exco semalam ditujukan kepada semua pihak bukan sahaja menteri besar dan barisan exconya.
Sewajarnya, titah Tuanku Muhriz mengandungi banyak peringatan dan nasihat kepada exco tetapi yang ingin saya ketengahkan di sini ialah saranan baginda kepada ‘semua pihak’.
Yang Dipertuan Besar bertitah semua pihak menjadikan segala peristiwa dan isu yang tercetus baru-baru ini sebagai satu pengajaran.
“Beta tidak mahu perkara yang sama berulang sehingga boleh menjejaskan keharmonian, kestabilan dan kelancaran pentadbiran negeri,” titah baginda.
Benar. Negeri Sembilan certainly does not need another crisis.

6e4a28ae4893a8ee: From Abdolreza Alami
The passing of Chandra Muzaffar on Nov 27 at the age of 79 marks the loss of one of Malaysia’s most distinctive public intellectuals, whose voice extended far beyond Malaysia.

For Iranians who live and work in Malaysia, Chandra represented a remarkable intellectual bridge between Southeast Asia and West Asia, between Islamic thought and universal human values, and between national sovereignty and global justice.

With international affairs increasingly shaped by geopolitical rivalries, selective interpretations of human rights and competing media narratives, his writings consistently returned to a fundamental question: should international relations be governed by power or moral principles?
A Malaysian intellectual with a global conscience
Born in Kedah in 1947, Chandra devoted nearly five decades to scholarship, social activism and public discourse.

In 1977, he founded Aliran, a multiethnic social reform movement committed to justice, freedom and solidarity. His academic career included positions at Universiti Sains Malaysia and Universiti Malaya, where he became the first director of the Centre for Civilisational Dialogue.
Through the International Movement for a Just World (JUST), he brought his intellectual concerns to an international audience.

His books, including Human Rights and the New World Order, Universalism of Islam and Global Ethic or Global Hegemony? reflected an intellectual commitment to understanding the relationship between ethics, political authority and international inequality.

What distinguished Chandra was his ability to connect Malaysia’s domestic concerns about social justice and multicultural coexistence with broader questions about the international distribution of power.
For him, justice was neither geographically confined nor the exclusive possession of any religious or political tradition.
Challenging the legacy of colonialism
Chandra understood that the end of formal colonial rule did not necessarily eliminate the structures of domination that shaped relations between nations.
He examined how unequal economic relationships, military intervention, political pressure and dominant media narratives could perpetuate dependencies long after countries had achieved independence.
His criticism of American foreign policy and Western hegemony was rooted in this broader intellectual framework.

Importantly, his critique was not a rejection of Western civilisation or its intellectual achievements. Rather, he questioned the concentration of power and inconsistencies between the principles proclaimed by powerful nations and their conduct in international affairs.

This perspective resonates with the historical experiences of both Malaysia and Iran, two societies whose understanding of sovereignty has been profoundly influenced by encounters with foreign intervention and imperial power.
Chandra’s advocacy of Malaysia’s non-aligned foreign policy reflected his belief in the importance of independent judgement in international affairs.
Palestine and the universality of justice

Few international issues occupied as prominent a place in Chandra’s writings as Palestine. He regarded Palestinian dispossession, occupation and displacement as fundamental questions of justice rather than merely matters of religious solidarity.
In an FMT article in January 2023, Chandra examined the importance of international institutions in addressing Palestinian rights.

During the Gaza war, he continued to emphasise the historical roots of the conflict, questioning approaches that addressed its immediate consequences without confronting the circumstances that had produced them.
His position also contained an important educational dimension. In November 2023, he told FMT that educators needed a comprehensive and unbiased understanding of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

For a scholar of media and communication, this aspect of his work is particularly significant. Public understanding of conflicts depends not only on what is reported but also on which historical experiences, perspectives and voices are included or excluded.
Chandra recognised that understanding Palestine required both historical knowledge and intellectual honesty.
Understanding Iran beyond familiar narratives
As an Iranian academic based in Malaysia, I find Chandra’s engagement with Iran particularly noteworthy.

He approached Iran not simply through the familiar frameworks of nuclear disputes, sanctions, religious differences or regional rivalries, but through its historical experience and aspirations for political independence.
In his 2012 article, Iran: The Price of Resistance, he examined the pressures confronting Iran in relation to its opposition to American dominance and Israeli policies in West Asia.
He placed tensions between Washington and Tehran within the wider context of regional power struggles, the consequences of the 1979 Islamic Revolution and Iran’s commitment to the Palestinian cause.
He also examined the geopolitical significance of Iran’s relationships with regional actors, including Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Readers may disagree with aspects of his analysis or with Tehran's policies, but Chandra's contribution lay in bringing historical and geopolitical perspectives into a discussion often dominated by immediate security concerns.
His concern was not confined to the sovereignty of a particular country. It extended to the human, economic and cultural consequences of war.
Rejecting sectarianism
Another important dimension of Chandra’s legacy was his opposition to sectarian divisions within the Muslim world.
In 2013, through JUST, he initiated a joint appeal for an end to violence between Sunni and Shia Muslims by former prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad and former Iranian president Mohammad Khatami.
He also advocated recognition of the Amman Message, which acknowledges the legitimacy of different Islamic schools of jurisprudence.
For Iranians living in Malaysia, his willingness to discuss these sensitive issues through scholarship and dialogue was especially meaningful.
Chandra understood that theological differences need not become political hostilities and that religious identity should not prevent mutual understanding.
An intellectual bridge worth remembering
Chandra’s legacy offers a valuable perspective on relations between Malaysia and Iran.
Diplomatic and economic relations are important, but enduring understanding between nations also develops through universities, intellectual exchanges, cultural engagement and independent media.
His work demonstrated the contribution Malaysian intellectuals can make to conversations about global affairs, including those concerning regions geographically distant from Southeast Asia.
He was not a figure whose every political position commanded universal agreement. Nor should an intellectual tribute require such agreement.
The enduring value of his work lies in the questions he raised, the historical perspectives he introduced and his willingness to engage with difficult subjects.

Malaysia has lost a distinguished scholar. Iran has lost an intellectual who sought to understand its historical experience. And the wider international community has lost a persistent advocate of dialogue and global justice.
His passing reminds us that intellectual independence, historical understanding and empathy remain indispensable in an increasingly divided world.
May his soul rest in peace. Al-Fatihah.
Abdolreza Alami is a geopolitical strategist, a senior lecturer, a researcher and an FMT reader.

b15b9da336f3059a: NEW YORK, Nov 28 — Wall Street ended higher yesterday, closing out a shortened trading week marked by both a surge in stock indexes and heavy selling of technology shares. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.18 per cent, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 2.31 per cent and the broad-based S&P 500 advanced 1.60 per cent. After shutting for Thanksgiving on Thursday, US markets closed early yesterday, at 1800 GMT. As Black Friday shopping got underway, online retail giant Amazon gained 3.96 per cent. The biggest gains came from stocks directly linked to artificial intelligence, including chipmakers Micron and AMD. Memory specialist SanDisk surged nearly 16 per cent. Only tech giant Nvidia, still at the center of a potential AI chip smuggling case, posted more modest gains, edging up just 0.80 per cent. "Weakness in Nvidia has done little to impede the broader AI trade's rebound," analysts at Briefing.com said. The sector came under heavy pressure in November amid concerns over the profitability of investments in AI development, fears of tighter regulation and questions raised by revelations involving Nvidia and its chief executive Jensen Huang. Only Huang's return to the helm of the company on Monday, less than two weeks after his resignation over extramarital affairs including with a suspected Chinese spy, helped the market recover, although trading remained volatile later in the week. The Nasdaq remains 12 per cent below its record high, reached early in the autumn. "The underlying concerns have not gone away. Questions over AI investment returns, financing costs and data-center spending remain unanswered," warned Fawad Razaqzada, an analyst at Forex.com. "The recovery needs fundamental support to become more than a relief rally." Friday's rally helped Anthropic regain some ground, allowing it to close above its initial listing price. After a record-breaking debut on the New York Stock Exchange on November 19, the AI startup had plunged, wiping hundreds of billions of dollars off its market capitalization. In the bond market, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to 4.93 per cent, from 4.85 per cent at Wednesday's close. Looking ahead to next week, investors will be watching several US economic indicators, particularly employment data, as well as Jensen Huang's testimony before Congress. — AFP

b209d4f26721c227: I recently returned from the UK where I got a sharp and depressing insight into economic, social and political developments both at home and around Europe on the daily news.

The town centre of Liverpool, where I grew up, was truly dismal. Once vibrant high-end retail outlets packed with shoppers were derelict and boarded up. The main shopping street was lined with people living in tents, fighting against the rain and cold and settling down to sleep for the remains of the day in the middle of the afternoon.

The high-street stores had gone and were replaced by discount stores, and the Cavern Walks and Matthew Street boutiques decked with murals of the Beatles were empty of shoppers. There was a general sense of an economy and society in deep distress.

On the television, Europe was struggling with riots in Paris, a mass shooting in Krakow and widespread demonstrations against the cost of living in other major cities. There were cyberattacks on refrigeration systems, not just melting groceries but more seriously damaging medical storage systems. Short-haul flights were grounded almost every day by hoax bomb threats with no obvious culprits identified.

The authorities did not appear to know or even care whether this was state-sponsored terrorism, religious fundamentalists or right-wing agitators disrupting day-to-day life and testing civil defences and responsiveness.

Amid this clearly depressing scenario, European politicians seemed oblivious to the impact on morale and the sense of well-being. The new Labour prime minister in the UK was resurrecting the futile debate on Britain’s membership of the EU. Within the EU, their own leaders were desperately trying to distract attention from the obvious decline of their authority by pointing at US president Donald Trump, the Middle East or the conflict in the Ukraine as the cause of all the problems.

There is something very seriously wrong, and from everything I saw and everyone I spoke to, people are fully aware of it but have no explanation, diagnosis or prescription to cure the malaise that is rapidly taking over an entire continent.

It was refreshing to return home to Malaysia, where the familiar debates are well-understood, and the first question I had to face in public was whether Malaysia can navigate these geopolitical tensions and global headwinds.

My answer was simple: Malaysia is navigating the geopolitical tensions and global headwinds very well already and should focus on the successes here at home without being distracted by the problems overseas.

The Malaysian economy, along with other Asian counterparts, is doing just fine. Under the unity government, the economy is growing well above the 4.0%-5.0% forecast at the start of the year and will likely grow 5.6%-5.7% this year. This is despite the conflict in the Middle East, the new Trump tariffs and the volatility in financial markets.

Inflation is under control and the ringgit is strong, thanks to good monetary policy management by Bank Negara. Foreign and domestic investment approvals and outcomes are meeting targets, and total trade and trade surplus are both at record levels.

The concern, which is real, remains the sense that even with this good economic performance, people are still struggling with the cost of living. This is the challenge facing Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim for the remainder of his term.

Malaysia knows how to create value but has not yet found the formula to share that value widely enough for him to take credit for the undoubted economic success his government has delivered. Unless he can do that quickly, the political uncertainty will certainly make him a one-term prime minister.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
861b047d04358d59: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 28 — OpenAI countersued Apple on Friday, alleging that the iPhone maker committed similar trade secret theft that it had accused the ChatGPT provider of this summer.
OpenAI alleged that Apple was stealing trade secrets through a former employee and pressuring shared suppliers to hamper its entry into the connected devices market.
An Apple spokesperson denounced the filing as “a transparent attempt to distract from the substance” of its own lawsuit.

The countersuit came in a filing Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, as part of the lawsuit filed by Apple in July against OpenAI and two of its employees who previously worked for Apple.

The two companies, partners since ChatGPT was integrated into Apple products in 2024, are poised to become rivals: OpenAI is developing its first connected devices designed for artificial intelligence with the studio of Jony Ive, Apple’s renowned former design chief.
Apple is seeking “to compete unfairly by any means available,” OpenAI’s lawyers wrote.
According to the filing, Apple is demanding that suppliers identify their projects for OpenAI and the employees assigned to them.
“Suppliers have expressed fear of losing Apple business and have moved or rescheduled meetings with OpenAI to avoid Apple seeing them,” the filing says.
One supplier moved OpenAI’s production to a night shift, while another dropped planned work “because of threats from Apple,” according to the filing, which does not name any of the firms.

OpenAI also accused a former Apple employee, who spent six months at OpenAI before leaving in June and returning to the iPhone maker, of sending “dozens of OpenAI documents” about a prototype to his personal phone numbers, then presenting OpenAI’s plans to senior Apple staff in July “at Apple’s request.”
The lawyers also challenged a clause barring former Apple employees who joined OpenAI from trying to poach their former colleagues for one year.

They also challenged a practice that allegedly encourages Apple employees to mix work files with their personal iCloud accounts so that, according to the lawyers, the company can later accuse those who leave of theft.

“This case is about OpenAI employees deliberately stealing, accessing, and using Apple’s secret and confidential information regarding our unreleased technologies, processes, and products - not about inadvertent retention of Apple information,” the Apple spokesperson said, on the condition AFP did not attribute the quote to a specific name.
OpenAI on Friday also withdrew its motion to dismiss the case, without giving a reason.
In October, OpenAI pledged not to use the information Apple claims as trade secrets, after the judge said he was “highly likely” to issue an order barring OpenAI from using it until trial. — AFP
09a52fc0b89a5262: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Berhad posted its highest quarterly profit in five years as net profit rose 12 per cent year-on-year to RM129 million in the third quarter ended September 30.
In a statement, Takaful Malaysia said quarterly takaful revenue rose 28 per cent to RM1.16 billion from RM902.8 million a year earlier.
The group declared an interim dividend of 20.5 sen per share, its highest in a decade and up 11 per cent from 18.5 sen last year.

“The record 20.5 sen dividend reflects our commitment to rewarding shareholders while preserving the financial capacity to support future business opportunities,” Takaful Malaysia group chief executive officer Nor Azman Zainal said.
For the nine months ended September 30, takaful revenue rose 14 per cent to RM3.14 billion from RM2.75 billion a year earlier, while net profit grew 8 per cent.
Profit before zakat and tax rose 6 per cent to RM497.8 million over the same period.
Family takaful revenue grew 14 per cent to RM1.85 billion, supported by higher contribution releases from the employee benefits business and higher charges for takaful coverage.
General takaful revenue rose 17 per cent to RM1.23 billion from RM1.05 billion a year earlier, driven mainly by higher contributions from its motor and fire segments.
Takaful Malaysia said its family retail business, launched in 2022, remained a priority, with growth of more than 30 per cent in its regular-contribution family takaful business.
The group is also expanding direct sales through Kaotim and its branch network and plans to introduce MediAsas in early 2027 to widen access to affordable medical coverage.
